questions.option_d: React's Virtual DOM is stored on the server
questions.explanation: React's reconciliation algorithm (diffing): compare new Virtual DOM with previous, find differences, apply minimum necessary real DOM operations. This makes React performant — actual DOM manipulation is the expensive part.

questions.statement: What does HTTP stand for in web development?
questions.option_a: HyperText Transfer Process
questions.option_b: HyperText Transfer Protocol
questions.option_c: HyperText Transmission Program
questions.option_d: HyperText Transport Protocol
questions.explanation: HTTP stands for HyperText Transfer Protocol, the foundation of data communication on the World Wide Web. The other options use the same initials but substitute incorrect words.

questions.statement: A web developer notices that their CSS background color change is not reflecting in the browser despite saving the file. Which is the most likely cause?
questions.option_a: The HTML file has a syntax error in the title tag
questions.option_b: The browser is serving a cached version of the old CSS file
questions.option_c: The web server does not support CSS3 properties
questions.option_d: The CSS selector specificity is lower than the HTML inline style
questions.explanation: Browsers cache static files like CSS to improve performance. When styles don't update despite saving, a stale cache is the most common cause, resolved by a hard refresh or clearing the cache.

questions.statement: Which HTML element is the correct semantic choice for the main navigation links of a website?
questions.option_a: <div id='nav'>
questions.option_b: <header>
questions.option_c: <nav>
questions.option_d: <section>
questions.explanation: The <nav> element is the HTML5 semantic element specifically designed to contain major navigation links. Using <div> with an id is non-semantic and provides no meaning to browsers or assistive technologies.

questions.statement: What does CSS stand for in web development?
questions.option_a: Cascading Style Sheets
questions.option_b: Computer Style Syntax
questions.option_c: Creative Style System
questions.option_d: Cascading Syntax Sheets
questions.explanation: CSS stands for Cascading Style Sheets, the language used to describe the presentation and styling of HTML documents. The other options are fabricated expansions of the same initials.

questions.statement: A React application renders a list of 10,000 items and users report the UI freezing when scrolling. Which optimization technique would most effectively address this?
questions.option_a: Increasing the browser's memory allocation limit
questions.option_b: Switching from React class components to functional components
questions.option_c: Implementing virtual scrolling or list virtualization
questions.option_d: Adding a CSS will-change property to the list container
questions.explanation: Virtual scrolling (list virtualization) renders only the items currently visible in the viewport, reducing DOM nodes from thousands to a few dozen. This dramatically improves scrolling performance for large lists.

questions.statement: Which HTTP status code indicates that a requested resource has been permanently moved to a new URL?
questions.option_a: 302 Found
questions.option_b: 304 Not Modified
questions.option_c: 301 Moved Permanently
questions.option_d: 307 Temporary Redirect
questions.explanation: 301 Moved Permanently tells the client and search engines that the resource has permanently moved to the URL specified in the Location header. 302 and 307 indicate temporary redirects.

questions.statement: What is the purpose of the 'DOCTYPE' declaration at the beginning of an HTML document?
questions.option_a: To link the HTML file to its external CSS stylesheet
questions.option_b: To define the character encoding for the page content
questions.option_c: To instruct the browser to render the document in standards mode
questions.option_d: To specify the server-side programming language used
questions.explanation: The <!DOCTYPE html> declaration tells the browser to render the page in full standards mode, preventing it from switching to quirks mode which uses outdated rendering rules. It is not a tag but a document type instruction.

questions.statement: A developer wants to center a div horizontally and vertically within its parent container without knowing the child's dimensions. Which CSS approach is the most modern and concise solution?
questions.option_a: Using position:absolute with margin:auto
questions.option_b: Using display:table-cell with vertical-align:middle
questions.option_c: Using display:flex with justify-content:center and align-items:center on the parent
questions.option_d: Using a combination of padding and text-align:center
questions.explanation: CSS Flexbox with justify-content:center (horizontal) and align-items:center (vertical) on the parent container centers a child element regardless of its dimensions. This is the most modern, concise approach that works without knowing the child's size.

questions.statement: What does the Same-Origin Policy (SOP) prevent in web browsers?
questions.option_a: JavaScript from manipulating CSS styles of elements on the same page
questions.option_b: A web page from loading resources from its own domain
questions.option_c: A script on one origin from reading data from a different origin without explicit permission
questions.option_d: Cookies from being sent with cross-site form submissions
questions.explanation: The Same-Origin Policy restricts how a document or script from one origin can interact with resources from a different origin, preventing malicious sites from reading sensitive data from other sites via JavaScript.

questions.statement: Which JavaScript method is used to execute a function after a specified delay, only once?
questions.option_a: setInterval()
questions.option_b: clearTimeout()
questions.option_c: setTimeout()
questions.option_d: requestAnimationFrame()
questions.explanation: setTimeout() executes a callback function once after a specified delay in milliseconds. setInterval() repeatedly executes a function at a given interval. requestAnimationFrame() synchronizes with the browser's repaint cycle.

questions.statement: A developer finds that their website scores poorly on the Core Web Vitals metric 'Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS)'. What does a high CLS score indicate?
questions.option_a: The page takes too long to respond to user interactions
questions.option_b: Visual elements move unexpectedly during page load causing poor user experience
questions.option_c: The main content of the page takes too long to render initially
questions.option_d: The total page size exceeds the recommended threshold
questions.explanation: CLS measures visual instability—how much unexpected layout shifting occurs during page load. A high CLS score means elements like text, buttons, or images are moving around after the initial render, disrupting the user experience.

questions.statement: What is the primary purpose of a Content Delivery Network (CDN) in web performance?
questions.option_a: To provide a backend database closer to the application server
questions.option_b: To distribute static assets across geographically dispersed servers to reduce latency
questions.option_c: To encrypt HTTPS traffic between the browser and the origin server
questions.option_d: To render server-side HTML pages closer to the user's location
questions.explanation: A CDN stores copies of static assets (images, CSS, JS) on servers geographically distributed around the world, serving them from the location closest to the user to reduce latency and improve load times.

questions.statement: Which CSS property is used to make an element visually hidden but still accessible to screen readers?
questions.option_a: display: none
questions.option_b: visibility: hidden
questions.option_c: opacity: 0
questions.option_d: position: absolute; clip: rect(0,0,0,0)
questions.explanation: Positioning an element with clip-rect or the modern clip-path approach hides it visually while keeping it in the DOM and accessible to assistive technologies. display:none and visibility:hidden remove the element from the accessibility tree.

questions.statement: What does REST stand for in the context of web APIs?
questions.option_a: Remote Execution and State Transfer
questions.option_b: Representational State Transfer
questions.option_c: Resource Endpoint Stateless Transfer
questions.option_d: Routing Engine for Scalable Transactions
questions.explanation: REST stands for Representational State Transfer, an architectural style for distributed hypermedia systems that defines constraints for creating scalable web services. The other options are fabricated expansions.

questions.statement: A developer is building a form where the user selects their country from a dropdown list of 200 options. Which HTML element and attribute combination is most appropriate?
questions.option_a: <input type='radio'> for each country option
questions.option_b: <select> with <option> elements inside
questions.option_c: <input type='text'> with a datalist element
questions.option_d: <ul> with <li> elements and click handlers
questions.explanation: A <select> element with nested <option> elements is the standard, accessible HTML control for choosing one value from a predefined list. A <datalist> supports autocomplete suggestions but allows free-text entry.

questions.statement: Which JavaScript concept allows a function to access variables from its enclosing scope even after the outer function has returned?
questions.option_a: Hoisting
questions.option_b: Prototype Chain
questions.option_c: Closure
questions.option_d: Callback
questions.explanation: A closure is a function that retains access to variables in its lexical scope (enclosing function's scope) even after the outer function has finished executing. This is fundamental to JavaScript's functional programming capabilities.

questions.statement: A backend developer sets up an API endpoint that processes large datasets. When tested with concurrent users, the server runs out of memory. Which Node.js approach would most effectively handle large data processing without high memory usage?
questions.option_a: Increasing the Node.js heap memory with --max-old-space-size
questions.option_b: Using synchronous file reading to process data in order
questions.option_c: Using Streams to process data in chunks rather than loading it all into memory
questions.option_d: Spawning a new process for each concurrent request
questions.explanation: Node.js Streams process data in chunks, enabling the handling of large datasets without loading the entire dataset into memory. Increasing heap size is a temporary workaround that doesn't address the fundamental memory inefficiency.

questions.statement: What does SQL stand for in database management for web applications?
questions.option_a: Structured Query Language
questions.option_b: Sequential Query Listing
questions.option_c: Standard Query Linkage
questions.option_d: Structured Queue Language
questions.explanation: SQL stands for Structured Query Language, the standard language for managing and manipulating relational databases. The other options are fabricated expansions of the same initials.

questions.statement: Which HTTP method is semantically correct for submitting data to a server to create a new resource?
questions.option_a: GET
questions.option_b: PUT
questions.option_c: POST
questions.option_d: PATCH
questions.explanation: POST is the correct HTTP method for submitting data to create a new resource on the server. PUT is used for replacing an existing resource; PATCH is used for partial updates; GET is for retrieval only and should not have side effects.

questions.statement: A developer wants to store user preferences such as theme selection in the browser so they persist across sessions without sending the data to the server. Which browser API should they use?
questions.option_a: IndexedDB
questions.option_b: Session Storage
questions.option_c: Cookies
questions.option_d: Local Storage
questions.explanation: Local Storage persists data across browser sessions (even after the browser is closed and reopened) without expiration and does not automatically transmit data to the server. Session Storage is cleared when the browser session ends.

questions.statement: What is Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) in web security?
questions.option_a: An attack that injects malicious scripts into web pages viewed by users
questions.option_b: An attack that tricks authenticated users into unknowingly submitting malicious requests
questions.option_c: An attack that intercepts communication between a user and a server
questions.option_d: An attack that floods a server with requests to make it unavailable
questions.explanation: CSRF tricks an authenticated user's browser into sending unwanted requests to a web application they're already logged into, exploiting the trust the site has in the user's browser. XSS injects malicious scripts; the others describe MitM and DDoS attacks.

questions.statement: Which CSS box model property adds space inside the border of an element, between the border and the content?
questions.option_a: Margin
questions.option_b: Border-spacing
questions.option_c: Padding
questions.option_d: Outline
questions.explanation: Padding is the space between an element's content and its border (inside the border). Margin is the space outside the border between the element and its neighbors.

questions.statement: A web developer needs to make HTTP requests to an API hosted on a different domain from their frontend application. The browser blocks the request with a CORS error. What does CORS stand for?
questions.option_a: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing
questions.option_b: Cross-Origin Request Security
questions.option_c: Client-Origin Resource Specification
questions.option_d: Cross-Origin Routing System
questions.explanation: CORS stands for Cross-Origin Resource Sharing, a mechanism that uses HTTP headers to tell browsers whether to allow web applications at one origin to access resources from a different origin. The other options are fabricated expansions.

questions.statement: Which JavaScript Promise method runs all provided promises concurrently and resolves only when every promise resolves, or rejects immediately if any promise rejects?
questions.option_a: Promise.race()
questions.option_b: Promise.allSettled()
questions.option_c: Promise.any()
questions.option_d: Promise.all()
questions.explanation: Promise.all() takes an array of promises, runs them concurrently, and resolves when all resolve (returning an array of results), or rejects immediately if any single promise rejects. Promise.allSettled() waits for all to settle regardless of outcome.

questions.statement: A website serves a page with 80 small icon images, each requiring a separate HTTP request. Which performance optimization would most effectively reduce the number of HTTP requests?
questions.option_a: Enabling browser-side caching for the icons
questions.option_b: Converting all icons to PNG format
questions.option_c: Using CSS sprites or an SVG icon sprite
questions.option_d: Increasing the server's connection pool size
questions.explanation: CSS sprites combine multiple images into one file, reducing 80 HTTP requests to one. SVG sprites similarly bundle multiple icons. Caching helps on repeat visits but doesn't reduce the initial request count.

questions.statement: What is the purpose of the HTML <meta charset='UTF-8'> tag?
questions.option_a: To define the language of the HTML document for SEO purposes
questions.option_b: To specify the character encoding used to correctly render text including special characters
questions.option_c: To set the viewport dimensions for responsive design on mobile devices
questions.option_d: To prevent search engines from indexing the page
questions.explanation: The charset meta tag declares the character encoding of the HTML document, ensuring the browser correctly renders special and international characters. UTF-8 is the recommended encoding as it supports virtually all characters.

questions.statement: In CSS, which selector has the highest specificity?
questions.option_a: A class selector (.my-class)
questions.option_b: An element type selector (div)
questions.option_c: An inline style attribute
questions.option_d: An ID selector (#my-id)
questions.explanation: Inline styles applied directly to an HTML element via the style attribute have the highest specificity among regular selectors (1,0,0,0), overriding ID selectors (0,1,0,0), class selectors (0,0,1,0), and element selectors (0,0,0,1).

questions.statement: A developer is debugging a JavaScript application and notices that a variable declared with var inside a for-loop is accessible outside the loop. What JavaScript concept explains this behavior?
questions.option_a: Closure
questions.option_b: Block Scoping
questions.option_c: Hoisting and Function Scoping
questions.option_d: Temporal Dead Zone
questions.explanation: Variables declared with var are function-scoped, not block-scoped, meaning they are accessible throughout the enclosing function regardless of where they are declared. let and const are block-scoped and would not be accessible outside the loop.

questions.statement: Which web architecture pattern separates the frontend and backend completely, with the frontend consuming data through API calls?
questions.option_a: Server-Side Rendering (SSR)
questions.option_b: Multi-Page Application (MPA)
questions.option_c: Decoupled/Headless Architecture
questions.option_d: Traditional Monolithic Architecture
questions.explanation: A Decoupled or Headless architecture completely separates the frontend presentation layer from the backend data and logic, with the frontend consuming data through API calls. SSR still has backend involvement in rendering HTML.

questions.statement: What does the acronym DOM stand for in web development?
questions.option_a: Document Object Manager
questions.option_b: Data Object Model
questions.option_c: Document Object Model
questions.option_d: Dynamic Object Manipulation
questions.explanation: DOM stands for Document Object Model, a programming interface for HTML and XML documents that represents the page as a tree of objects. JavaScript uses the DOM to dynamically read and manipulate page content and structure.

questions.statement: A developer runs Lighthouse on their web application and gets a low 'Time to Interactive' (TTI) score. Which optimization would most directly improve TTI?
questions.option_a: Adding more descriptive alt attributes to images
questions.option_b: Reducing and deferring render-blocking JavaScript
questions.option_c: Increasing the color contrast ratio of text elements
questions.option_d: Using semantic HTML5 elements instead of divs
questions.explanation: TTI measures how long until a page is fully interactive. Large, render-blocking JavaScript bundles are the primary cause of high TTI. Code splitting, deferring non-critical scripts, and lazy loading significantly improve this metric.

questions.statement: Which HTTP header instructs the browser to only access the site over HTTPS and remember this for a specified duration?
questions.option_a: Content-Security-Policy
questions.option_b: X-Frame-Options
questions.option_c: Strict-Transport-Security
questions.option_d: X-XSS-Protection
questions.explanation: The Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS) header tells browsers to always use HTTPS for the domain and to remember this policy for the specified max-age, preventing downgrade attacks. CSP controls what resources can be loaded.

questions.statement: What is the main difference between localStorage and sessionStorage in the Web Storage API?
questions.option_a: localStorage stores data as JSON objects; sessionStorage stores only strings
questions.option_b: localStorage persists after the browser is closed; sessionStorage is cleared when the tab is closed
questions.option_c: localStorage is accessible across all tabs; sessionStorage is accessible only to the origin domain
questions.option_d: localStorage encrypts data automatically; sessionStorage stores data in plain text
questions.explanation: The key difference is persistence: localStorage data survives browser restarts and persists until explicitly cleared, while sessionStorage data is cleared when the browser tab or window is closed. Both store data as strings.

questions.statement: A React developer notices that a child component re-renders every time the parent renders, even though the child's props have not changed. Which React hook should be used to prevent this unnecessary re-rendering?
questions.option_a: useEffect
questions.option_b: useCallback
questions.option_c: useRef
questions.option_d: useMemo
questions.explanation: useCallback memoizes callback functions so that the same function reference is passed to child components on each render, preventing unnecessary re-renders of child components that use React.memo. useMemo memoizes computed values.

questions.statement: What does the acronym API stand for in the context of web development?
questions.option_a: Application Process Integration
questions.option_b: Advanced Programming Interface
questions.option_c: Application Programming Interface
questions.option_d: Automated Page Interface
questions.explanation: API stands for Application Programming Interface, a set of definitions and protocols for building and integrating application software. In web development, it typically refers to web APIs that allow frontend code to communicate with backend services.

questions.statement: Which CSS feature allows developers to apply different styles based on the characteristics of the user's device, such as screen width?
questions.option_a: CSS Variables
questions.option_b: CSS Transforms
questions.option_c: CSS Media Queries
questions.option_d: CSS Grid
questions.explanation: CSS Media Queries apply different CSS rules based on device characteristics like viewport width, height, or resolution, forming the foundation of responsive web design. CSS Variables store reusable values; Grid is a layout system.

questions.statement: A web application stores user passwords by simply converting them to MD5 hashes. Why is this a critical security vulnerability?
questions.option_a: MD5 is not a valid hashing algorithm recognized by modern browsers
questions.option_b: MD5 hashes are reversible using simple decryption algorithms
questions.option_c: MD5 is cryptographically broken and vulnerable to collision and rainbow table attacks
questions.option_d: MD5 hashes are too long to store efficiently in a database
questions.explanation: MD5 is cryptographically broken: it is fast (making brute force easy), vulnerable to collision attacks, and rainbow table attacks can instantly reverse common passwords. Secure password storage requires slow, salted algorithms like bcrypt or Argon2.

questions.statement: In JavaScript, which keyword declares a variable that is block-scoped and cannot be re-assigned after its initial declaration?
questions.option_a: var
questions.option_b: let
questions.option_c: const
questions.option_d: static
questions.explanation: const declares a block-scoped variable binding that cannot be re-assigned (though the object it references can still be mutated). let is block-scoped but allows re-assignment. var is function-scoped and allows both.

questions.statement: What is the purpose of a 'webhook' in web integration?
questions.option_a: A JavaScript hook that runs before a DOM event is processed
questions.option_b: A server-to-server callback mechanism that sends real-time data when an event occurs
questions.option_c: A browser API for intercepting network requests
questions.option_d: A CSS pseudo-element that applies styles on hover
questions.explanation: A webhook is an HTTP callback that allows a server to send real-time data to another server when a specific event occurs, without the receiving server needing to poll for updates. It is a push-based integration mechanism.

questions.statement: Which CSS layout system is best suited for creating two-dimensional layouts with rows and columns simultaneously?
questions.option_a: Flexbox
questions.option_b: Float-based Layout
questions.option_c: CSS Grid
questions.option_d: Multi-column Layout
questions.explanation: CSS Grid is designed specifically for two-dimensional layouts where both rows and columns can be controlled simultaneously. Flexbox is primarily a one-dimensional layout system, aligning items along a single axis at a time.

questions.statement: A developer uses the following code: fetch('/api/data').then(res => res.json()).then(data => console.log(data)). What is the purpose of the res.json() call?
questions.option_a: It validates that the response data conforms to a JSON schema
questions.option_b: It parses the response body from a JSON-formatted string into a JavaScript object
questions.option_c: It serializes a JavaScript object into a JSON string for storage
questions.option_d: It checks whether the HTTP response status code is 200 OK
questions.explanation: res.json() reads the HTTP response body stream and parses it as JSON, returning a Promise that resolves with the resulting JavaScript object. It is a convenience method of the Fetch API's Response object.

questions.statement: What is SQL Injection and why is it dangerous?
questions.option_a: A technique to optimize database queries by injecting index hints
questions.option_b: An attack where malicious SQL code is inserted into input fields to manipulate the database
questions.option_c: A method of injecting test data into a database during development
questions.option_d: An SQL optimization technique for handling large BLOB data
questions.explanation: SQL Injection occurs when an attacker inserts malicious SQL code into an input field that is concatenated into a database query, potentially reading, modifying, or deleting data. It is dangerous because it can compromise an entire database.

questions.statement: Which HTML attribute is essential for making form input fields accessible to screen readers when no visible label is present?
questions.option_a: placeholder
questions.option_b: name
questions.option_c: aria-label
questions.option_d: title
questions.explanation: The aria-label attribute provides a text label for interactive elements that have no visible on-screen label, making them accessible to screen reader users. The placeholder attribute disappears when the user types and should not be used as a substitute for a label.

questions.statement: A developer wants to prevent a website from being embedded in an iframe on another domain to protect against clickjacking attacks. Which HTTP response header achieves this?
questions.option_a: Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'
questions.option_b: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
questions.option_c: Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000
questions.option_d: X-Frame-Options: DENY
questions.explanation: The X-Frame-Options: DENY header prevents the page from being embedded in any iframe, protecting users from clickjacking. CSP with frame-ancestors is the modern equivalent, but X-Frame-Options is widely supported and commonly used.

questions.statement: What is the difference between == and === in JavaScript?
questions.option_a: == compares values and types; === compares only values
questions.option_b: == uses strict comparison; === uses loose comparison
questions.option_c: == performs type coercion before comparison; === checks both value and type without coercion
questions.option_d: == only works with primitive types; === works with all types
questions.explanation: The == operator performs type coercion (converting operands to a common type before comparison), which can lead to unexpected results like 0 == false being true. The === strict equality operator compares both value and type without coercion.

questions.statement: Which backend architecture pattern involves each request being handled independently without the server storing any information about the client's previous requests?
questions.option_a: Session-Based Architecture
questions.option_b: Stateful Architecture
questions.option_c: Stateless Architecture
questions.option_d: Cookie-Based Architecture
questions.explanation: Stateless architecture means the server does not retain any client state between requests. Each request contains all information needed to process it. This simplifies scaling because any server instance can handle any request.

questions.statement: A web developer needs to apply a CSS transition that animates only on GPU-composited properties for the smoothest performance. Which properties should they animate?
questions.option_a: width and height
questions.option_b: top and left
questions.option_c: opacity and transform
questions.option_d: font-size and padding
questions.explanation: Animating opacity and transform triggers GPU compositing, bypassing the main thread layout and paint steps. Animating width, height, top, left, font-size, or padding triggers expensive layout recalculations on the main thread.

questions.statement: What does the acronym SPA stand for in modern web development?
questions.option_a: Server-Page Application
questions.option_b: Single-Page Application
questions.option_c: Scripted Page Architecture
questions.option_d: Single-Process Application
questions.explanation: SPA stands for Single-Page Application, a web application that loads a single HTML page and dynamically updates content using JavaScript, without full page reloads. React, Angular, and Vue.js are commonly used to build SPAs.

questions.statement: A developer writes a Node.js route that reads a large file synchronously before sending a response. How does this affect server performance under concurrent requests?
questions.option_a: It has no effect because Node.js handles all operations on separate threads
questions.option_b: It improves performance by ensuring file data is fully loaded before processing
questions.option_c: It blocks the event loop, causing all concurrent requests to wait until the read completes
questions.option_d: It automatically delegates the read to a worker thread to prevent blocking
questions.explanation: Node.js uses a single-threaded event loop. Synchronous (blocking) operations like fs.readFileSync() block the entire event loop, preventing all other requests from being processed until the operation completes.

questions.statement: Which CSS property controls the stacking order of positioned elements along the z-axis?
questions.option_a: position
questions.option_b: display
questions.option_c: z-index
questions.option_d: overflow
questions.explanation: z-index controls the vertical stacking order of positioned elements (those with a position value other than static). Higher z-index values place elements in front of elements with lower values.

questions.statement: What is the purpose of the 'async' and 'await' keywords in JavaScript?
questions.option_a: To declare variables that are automatically updated when their values change
questions.option_b: To run JavaScript code in parallel on multiple CPU cores
questions.option_c: To write asynchronous Promise-based code in a synchronous-looking style
questions.option_d: To define functions that execute immediately upon being declared
questions.explanation: async/await is syntactic sugar over Promises that allows asynchronous code to be written in a sequential, synchronous-looking style, making it easier to read and maintain. It does not enable true parallelism in JavaScript.

questions.statement: In web security, what is 'input validation' and why is it considered a server-side responsibility?
questions.option_a: Checking if a user's input matches the expected format to improve UI appearance, done only in the browser
questions.option_b: Verifying that submitted data meets expected format, type, and range constraints, enforced on the server because client-side validation can be bypassed
questions.option_c: Escaping HTML characters in output to prevent XSS, performed by the rendering engine
questions.option_d: Sanitizing database queries to prevent SQL injection at the ORM level
questions.explanation: Input validation on the server verifies that all submitted data is correct and safe. Client-side validation improves UX but can be bypassed by an attacker sending raw HTTP requests, making server-side enforcement mandatory for security.

questions.statement: Which HTML5 element should be used to represent a self-contained piece of content that could be independently distributed, such as a blog post or news article?
questions.option_a: <section>
questions.option_b: <aside>
questions.option_c: <article>
questions.option_d: <main>
questions.explanation: The <article> element represents a self-contained, independently distributable piece of content. <section> groups related content within a document but is not self-contained. <aside> represents tangentially related content.

questions.statement: A developer implements lazy loading for images on a webpage. What is the primary benefit of this technique?
questions.option_a: Images are decoded in a higher quality format before display
questions.option_b: Images are only loaded when they are about to enter the user's viewport, reducing initial page load time
questions.option_c: Images are stored in the browser cache permanently for instant future access
questions.option_d: Images are compressed automatically by the browser before downloading
questions.explanation: Lazy loading defers the loading of images until they are close to entering the viewport, reducing the initial page payload, speeding up the first meaningful paint, and saving bandwidth for images the user may never scroll to.

questions.statement: What does GraphQL offer over traditional REST APIs that makes it particularly useful for complex data requirements?
questions.option_a: It stores all data in a graph database for faster retrieval
questions.option_b: Clients can request exactly the fields they need, eliminating over-fetching and under-fetching
questions.option_c: It automatically generates database schemas from API queries
questions.option_d: It requires no server-side code, running entirely in the browser
questions.explanation: GraphQL allows clients to specify exactly what data they need in a single query, eliminating over-fetching (receiving more data than needed) and under-fetching (needing multiple requests to get all required data).

questions.statement: Which JavaScript event listener method is used to stop an event from propagating to parent elements?
questions.option_a: event.preventDefault()
questions.option_b: event.stopImmediatePropagation()
questions.option_c: event.stopPropagation()
questions.option_d: event.cancelBubble()
questions.explanation: event.stopPropagation() prevents the event from bubbling up the DOM tree to parent elements. event.preventDefault() prevents the default browser action (like following a link), not the propagation of the event.

questions.statement: A developer wants to ensure that a website's layout adapts gracefully to screens of all sizes, from mobile phones to desktops. Which approach starts with the smallest screen and progressively enhances for larger screens?
questions.option_a: Desktop-First Design
questions.option_b: Adaptive Design
questions.option_c: Progressive Enhancement
questions.option_d: Mobile-First Design
questions.explanation: Mobile-First Design starts by designing and coding for the smallest screen size, then uses CSS media queries with min-width to progressively add styles for larger screens. This approach prioritizes performance for mobile users.

questions.statement: What is the purpose of a service worker in Progressive Web Applications (PWAs)?
questions.option_a: To replace the web server with a local JavaScript execution environment
questions.option_b: To intercept network requests and enable offline functionality and push notifications
questions.option_c: To enhance CSS rendering performance by offloading work to a separate thread
questions.option_d: To provide a secure context for storing user authentication tokens
questions.explanation: Service workers are JavaScript files that run in the background, separate from the web page, intercepting network requests to implement caching strategies. This enables offline functionality, background sync, and push notifications in PWAs.

questions.statement: Which CSS pseudo-class selects an element only when it is being actively clicked by the user?
questions.option_a: ::hover
questions.option_b: ::focus
questions.option_c: ::active
questions.option_d: ::visited
questions.explanation: The :active pseudo-class applies styles to an element during the moment it is being activated, i.e., when a user clicks and holds down the mouse button. :hover applies when the cursor is over the element; :focus when it has keyboard focus.

questions.statement: A web application developer uses prepared statements (parameterized queries) when interacting with the database. Which attack does this most directly prevent?
questions.option_a: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
questions.option_b: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
questions.option_c: SQL Injection
questions.option_d: Clickjacking
questions.explanation: Prepared statements separate SQL code from user-supplied data, ensuring that user input is always treated as a data parameter and never as executable SQL code, directly preventing SQL Injection attacks.

questions.statement: What does the acronym AJAX stand for?
questions.option_a: Asynchronous JavaScript and XHTML
questions.option_b: Automated JavaScript and XML
questions.option_c: Asynchronous JavaScript and XML
questions.option_d: Advanced JavaScript API for XML
questions.explanation: AJAX stands for Asynchronous JavaScript and XML, a technique for making asynchronous HTTP requests from a browser without reloading the full page. Modern AJAX often uses JSON rather than XML, but the acronym remains standard.

questions.statement: A developer needs to redirect all HTTP traffic on port 80 to HTTPS on port 443 for their web application. At which layer is this redirect typically configured?
questions.option_a: In the JavaScript application code
questions.option_b: In the HTML meta refresh tag
questions.option_c: In the web server configuration (e.g., Nginx or Apache)
questions.option_d: In the browser's security settings
questions.explanation: HTTP-to-HTTPS redirects are standard web server configurations (e.g., an Nginx server block returning a 301 to the HTTPS URL). This is more efficient and reliable than application-level or HTML-level redirects.

questions.statement: Which Node.js module system keyword is used to import modules in modern ECMAScript (ES6+) syntax?
questions.option_a: require()
questions.option_b: include()
questions.option_c: import
questions.option_d: load()
questions.explanation: The import keyword is the ES6+ module system syntax for importing exported members from another module. require() is the CommonJS module system used in older Node.js code. ES6 import/export is now the standard.

questions.statement: What is the primary purpose of the robots.txt file in web development?
questions.option_a: To define CSS styles for robotic or automated browser testing
questions.option_b: To instruct search engine crawlers which pages they are allowed or not allowed to index
questions.option_c: To store automated test scripts for end-to-end browser testing
questions.option_d: To configure the web server to block unauthorized bot traffic
questions.explanation: The robots.txt file is placed at the root of a website to communicate with web crawlers and search engine bots, specifying which URLs the bot should and should not crawl or index. It is a convention, not a security mechanism.

questions.statement: In the context of web performance, what does 'code splitting' achieve?
questions.option_a: It splits a large team's codebase into separate Git repositories for each developer
questions.option_b: It divides a large JavaScript bundle into smaller chunks that are loaded on demand
questions.option_c: It automatically minifies JavaScript code during the build process
questions.option_d: It separates CSS files from JavaScript files during deployment
questions.explanation: Code splitting divides a large JavaScript bundle into smaller chunks that are loaded only when needed (e.g., when a user navigates to a specific route), reducing the initial JavaScript payload and improving page load time.

questions.statement: A developer's Express.js API is returning data correctly in Postman, but the React frontend receives a CORS error. What is the most appropriate fix?
questions.option_a: Change the React app's domain to match the Express server's domain
questions.option_b: Enable CORS headers on the Express server using the cors middleware or custom headers
questions.option_c: Disable the browser's security settings for local development
questions.option_d: Switch from using fetch() to XMLHttpRequest in the React frontend
questions.explanation: CORS errors are caused by the server not including the appropriate Access-Control-Allow-Origin header. The correct fix is to configure the Express server to send these headers, not to disable browser security or change the client.

questions.statement: Which design pattern is commonly implemented by frontend state management libraries like Redux?
questions.option_a: Model-View-Controller (MVC)
questions.option_b: Observer Pattern
questions.option_c: Flux/Unidirectional Data Flow
questions.option_d: Factory Pattern
questions.explanation: Redux implements the Flux/Unidirectional Data Flow pattern, where data flows in one direction: Actions trigger Reducers which update the Store, and the View re-renders based on the Store. This predictable data flow makes state changes easier to debug.

questions.statement: What is the purpose of semantic HTML in web development?
questions.option_a: To make web pages load faster by reducing the number of HTML tags
questions.option_b: To give meaning to the structure of web content for browsers, search engines, and assistive technologies
questions.option_c: To apply consistent styling across all HTML elements
questions.option_d: To enable JavaScript to access DOM elements without using class selectors
questions.explanation: Semantic HTML uses elements like <article>, <nav>, <header>, and <main> that convey the meaning and structure of content, improving accessibility for assistive technologies, SEO for search engines, and code readability for developers.

questions.statement:
A web developer wants to apply a style to all

elements that are direct children of a

with the class 'container'. Which CSS selector achieves this?
questions.option_a: div.container p
questions.option_b: div.container + p
questions.option_c: div.container ~ p
questions.option_d: div.container > p
questions.explanation:
The child combinator (>) selects elements that are direct children of the specified parent. div.container > p selects

elements that are direct children of

. The descendant selector (space) selects all descendants, not just direct children.

questions.statement: What does the 'defer' attribute on a <script> tag do?
questions.option_a: It prevents the script from ever being executed in the browser
questions.option_b: It downloads the script asynchronously and executes it after the HTML document has been fully parsed
questions.option_c: It executes the script inline before any HTML parsing begins
questions.option_d: It caches the script in service worker storage for offline use
questions.explanation: The defer attribute tells the browser to download the script in parallel with HTML parsing and execute it in order after the document has been fully parsed, preventing render-blocking behavior while maintaining script execution order.

questions.statement: In web development, what is 'server-side rendering' (SSR)?
questions.option_a: Running JavaScript logic on the server instead of the client to reduce bundle size
questions.option_b: Generating the full HTML of a page on the server before sending it to the client's browser
questions.option_c: Caching API responses on the server to reduce database queries
questions.option_d: Pre-rendering static HTML pages during the build process
questions.explanation: Server-Side Rendering generates the complete HTML for a page on the server for each request and sends it to the browser, which means the user sees content faster and search engines can index it without executing JavaScript.

questions.statement: A developer notices that their web page's images take a long time to load because they are being served in PNG format at very large dimensions. Which combination of optimizations would most directly reduce image load time?
questions.option_a: Changing the image CSS filter and adding alt text
questions.option_b: Compressing the images and serving them in WebP format with appropriate srcset dimensions
questions.option_c: Enabling lazy loading in JavaScript and adding aria-label attributes
questions.option_d: Moving image references from CSS to HTML img tags
questions.explanation: Serving images in the modern WebP format (smaller file sizes than PNG/JPEG at same quality) and using srcset to serve appropriately sized images for different devices directly reduces download size, the main factor in image load time.

questions.statement: Which JavaScript method returns a new array containing only the elements that pass a provided test function?
questions.option_a: map()
questions.option_b: reduce()
questions.option_c: find()
questions.option_d: filter()
questions.explanation: filter() creates a new array with all elements for which the provided function returns true. map() transforms elements without filtering; find() returns the first matching element; reduce() aggregates all elements into a single value.

questions.statement: What is the purpose of HTTPS compared to HTTP?
questions.option_a: HTTPS loads pages significantly faster than HTTP due to compression
questions.option_b: HTTPS encrypts the data transmitted between the browser and server using TLS
questions.option_c: HTTPS allows larger file uploads than HTTP
questions.option_d: HTTPS stores a copy of the page on the user's device for offline access
questions.explanation: HTTPS uses TLS (Transport Layer Security) to encrypt the communication between the browser and the web server, protecting data in transit from interception and tampering. HTTP transmits data in plain text.

questions.statement: A developer implements an authentication system using JSON Web Tokens (JWT). Where is the recommended location to store a JWT in a browser application for security?
questions.option_a: In localStorage for easy access across all browser tabs
questions.option_b: In sessionStorage to automatically expire on tab close
questions.option_c: In a URL query parameter for easy server-side access
questions.option_d: In an HttpOnly cookie to prevent JavaScript access
questions.explanation: Storing JWTs in HttpOnly cookies prevents client-side JavaScript from accessing them, protecting against XSS attacks that could steal tokens from localStorage or sessionStorage. The HttpOnly flag ensures the token is only sent with HTTP requests.

questions.statement: What does the acronym CSS Grid's 'fr' unit stand for and what does it represent?
questions.option_a: Fixed ratio; a proportion of the container fixed in pixels
questions.option_b: Fractional remainder; the space remaining after fixed elements are placed
questions.option_c: Flexible ratio; a dynamic percentage of the viewport
questions.option_d: Full row; defines a column that spans the entire grid width
questions.explanation: 'fr' stands for fractional unit, representing a fraction of the available free space in the grid container after fixed and content-based track sizes have been allocated. 1fr takes one equal share of the remaining space.

questions.statement: A user reports that clicking the 'Submit' button on a form causes the page to reload and the form data to be lost. What is the most likely cause?
questions.option_a: The form is missing a required id attribute
questions.option_b: The button does not have an onclick event handler
questions.option_c: The form's default submission behavior is not being prevented in the JavaScript handler
questions.option_d: The CSS display property of the button is set to inline
questions.explanation: A standard HTML form submit triggers a full page reload by default. If a JavaScript handler is attached to manage form submission via AJAX but event.preventDefault() is not called, the default reload behavior will execute.

questions.statement: Which tool is used in Node.js to manage project dependencies and run scripts defined in package.json?
questions.option_a: Webpack
questions.option_b: Babel
questions.option_c: npm (Node Package Manager)
questions.option_d: ESLint
questions.explanation: npm (Node Package Manager) is the default package manager for Node.js, used to install, update, and manage project dependencies listed in package.json, and to run project scripts. Webpack is a module bundler; Babel is a transpiler.

questions.statement: What is the purpose of the 'alt' attribute on an HTML element?
questions.option_a: To define the tooltip text displayed when hovering over the image
questions.option_b: To provide alternative text for screen readers and when the image fails to load
questions.option_c: To specify the source URL of a fallback image if the primary fails
questions.option_d: To set the image's dimensions for layout purposes
questions.explanation: The alt attribute provides alternative text that is read by screen readers for accessibility and displayed to users when the image fails to load. It is a critical accessibility requirement and also contributes to SEO.

questions.statement: Which CSS property creates a smooth visual transition when an element's property changes?
questions.option_a: animation
questions.option_b: transform
questions.option_c: transition
questions.option_d: keyframes
questions.explanation: The transition property defines a smooth change of a CSS property over a specified duration, easing function, and delay. The animation property enables more complex, keyframe-based animations that can loop and play automatically.

questions.statement: A company's website is experiencing a slowdown because the database is queried for the same user profile data on every single page request. Which technique would most effectively solve this?
questions.option_a: Switching from a relational to a NoSQL database
questions.option_b: Implementing server-side caching (e.g., Redis) to store frequently accessed data
questions.option_c: Increasing the number of available database connection threads
questions.option_d: Rewriting the database queries using stored procedures
questions.explanation: Server-side caching with a tool like Redis stores frequently accessed data in memory, allowing subsequent requests to be served from cache without hitting the database, dramatically reducing query load and response time.

questions.statement: What is the primary role of a bundler like Webpack in modern web development?
questions.option_a: To compress image files before uploading them to a CDN
questions.option_b: To combine multiple JavaScript and CSS files into optimized bundles for browser delivery
questions.option_c: To deploy web applications automatically to cloud hosting services
questions.option_d: To generate HTML pages statically from template files
questions.explanation: Webpack analyzes JavaScript module dependencies and bundles them into optimized output files for the browser, applying transformations like minification, code splitting, and tree-shaking to improve performance.

questions.statement: A developer uses CSS variables (custom properties). Which syntax correctly declares and uses a CSS variable?
questions.option_a: $primary-color: blue; color: $primary-color;
questions.option_b: @variable primary-color: blue; color: var(primary-color);
questions.option_c: --primary-color: blue; color: var(--primary-color);
questions.option_d: #primary-color: blue; color: use(#primary-color);
questions.explanation: CSS custom properties (variables) are declared with a double-dash prefix (--primary-color: blue) within a selector scope and referenced using the var() function (var(--primary-color)). The $syntax is SCSS/Sass, not native CSS.

questions.statement: In RESTful API design, which HTTP status code should be returned when a resource is successfully created?
questions.option_a: 200 OK
questions.option_b: 204 No Content
questions.option_c: 201 Created
questions.option_d: 202 Accepted
questions.explanation: 201 Created is the correct HTTP status code to return when a resource has been successfully created as a result of a POST request. 200 OK indicates a successful general response; 204 means success with no body to return.

questions.statement: What is the purpose of the 'viewport' meta tag commonly found in the HTML head of responsive web pages?
questions.option_a: To set the background color of the page before CSS loads
questions.option_b: To instruct the browser to scale and size the viewport correctly for the device's screen width
questions.option_c: To prevent search engine crawlers from indexing the mobile version
questions.option_d: To define the language and character direction of the page content
questions.explanation: The viewport meta tag (<meta name='viewport' content='width=device-width, initial-scale=1'>) instructs mobile browsers to set the viewport width to the device's actual screen width and set the initial zoom level, enabling proper responsive design rendering.

questions.statement: A frontend developer uses the React useEffect hook with an empty dependency array []. When does this effect run?
questions.option_a: On every render of the component
questions.option_b: Never, because the dependency array is empty
questions.option_c: Only once, after the first render (component mount)
questions.option_d: Only when the component's props change
questions.explanation: A useEffect with an empty dependency array ([]) runs once after the initial render (equivalent to componentDidMount in class components). It does not run on subsequent re-renders unless the component unmounts and remounts.

questions.statement: What does the term 'tree-shaking' refer to in modern JavaScript bundling?
questions.option_a: Removing unnecessary CSS rules from the final stylesheet
questions.option_b: Eliminating unused, dead code exports from JavaScript bundles during the build process
questions.option_c: Optimizing the DOM tree by removing elements with no visible content
questions.option_d: Clearing the browser's application cache during deployment
questions.explanation: Tree-shaking is the process of removing unused code exports from the final JavaScript bundle, reducing its size. Bundlers like Webpack analyze the import/export dependency graph and exclude code that is never imported or used.

questions.statement: Which web API allows JavaScript to make HTTP requests and returns a Promise-based interface?
questions.option_a: XMLHttpRequest
questions.option_b: axios
questions.option_c: The Fetch API
questions.option_d: The WebSocket API
questions.explanation: The Fetch API is a native browser API that provides a modern, Promise-based interface for making HTTP requests. XMLHttpRequest is the older, callback-based predecessor. Axios is a popular third-party library, not a native browser API.

questions.statement: A developer wants a CSS grid layout where each column is at least 200px wide but grows equally to fill the available space. Which CSS property value achieves this?
questions.option_a: repeat(auto-fill, 200px)
questions.option_b: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(200px, 1fr))
questions.option_c: repeat(4, 1fr)
questions.option_d: repeat(auto-fill, max-content)
questions.explanation: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(200px, 1fr)) creates a responsive grid where each column is at least 200px wide but grows equally (1fr) to fill available space, automatically adding or removing columns to fit the container width.

questions.statement: What is the difference between 'authentication' and 'authorization' in web security?
questions.option_a: Authentication checks what resources a user can access; authorization verifies their identity
questions.option_b: Authentication verifies who the user is; authorization determines what they are allowed to do
questions.option_c: Authentication uses passwords; authorization uses tokens exclusively
questions.option_d: Authentication applies to APIs; authorization applies only to web pages
questions.explanation: Authentication is the process of verifying a user's identity (proving who they are), while authorization is the process of determining what authenticated users are permitted to access or do. They are distinct but complementary security processes.

questions.statement: Which database concept ensures that a series of database operations either all succeed or all fail together, leaving the database in a consistent state?
questions.option_a: Indexing
questions.option_b: Foreign Key Constraint
questions.option_c: Transaction
questions.option_d: Normalization
questions.explanation: A database Transaction groups multiple operations into an atomic unit that either entirely succeeds (commits) or entirely fails (rolls back), ensuring data consistency. This is defined by ACID properties (Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability).

questions.statement: A web developer adds 'use strict'; at the top of a JavaScript file. What effect does this have?
questions.option_a: It enables ES6 features in older browsers automatically
questions.option_b: It prevents the browser from caching the JavaScript file
questions.option_c: It enables strict mode, which catches common JavaScript mistakes as errors
questions.option_d: It disables certain browser security policies for the file
questions.explanation: 'use strict' enables JavaScript's strict mode, which turns common programming mistakes into thrown errors (such as using undeclared variables), prevents the use of deprecated syntax, and makes it easier to write secure JavaScript.

questions.statement: What is the primary purpose of environment variables in web application deployment?
questions.option_a: To define CSS custom properties for different deployment environments
questions.option_b: To store configuration values like API keys and database URLs outside of the source code
questions.option_c: To specify the browser compatibility requirements for the application
questions.option_d: To configure the network firewall rules for the hosting server
questions.explanation: Environment variables store configuration values (API keys, database connection strings, feature flags) outside of the application's source code, allowing the same codebase to run with different configurations in development, staging, and production environments.

questions.statement: Which HTML form element creates a multi-line text input field?
questions.option_a: <input type='multiline'>
questions.option_b: <input type='text' rows='5'>
questions.option_c: <textfield>
questions.option_d: <textarea>
questions.explanation: <textarea> is the correct HTML element for multi-line text input. The <input> element is always a single-line control regardless of attributes like rows (which are not valid on <input>).

questions.statement: A developer is troubleshooting why changes deployed to a server are not reflected for users. After investigation, they find that a CDN is serving old versions of the static files. What is the standard technique to force CDNs and browsers to use the new files?
questions.option_a: Renaming the web server's IP address
questions.option_b: Appending a version hash or cache-busting query string to the asset filename or URL
questions.option_c: Increasing the HTTP Keep-Alive timeout on the server
questions.option_d: Switching from HTTPS to HTTP to bypass CDN caching
questions.explanation: Cache busting appends a unique version identifier (hash or version number) to asset filenames or URLs, causing browsers and CDNs to treat the file as a new resource and fetch it fresh, bypassing cached versions.

questions.statement: What does the 'position: absolute' CSS property do to an element?
questions.option_a: It fixes the element to the viewport so it does not scroll with the page
questions.option_b: It positions the element relative to the nearest positioned ancestor, removing it from normal document flow
questions.option_c: It aligns the element to the center of its parent container
questions.option_d: It positions the element relative to its normal position in the document flow
questions.explanation: position:absolute removes an element from the normal document flow and positions it relative to its nearest ancestor that has a position value other than static. position:fixed positions relative to the viewport.

questions.statement: Which HTTP method is idempotent and used to completely replace an existing resource on the server?
questions.option_a: POST
questions.option_b: DELETE
questions.option_c: PATCH
questions.option_d: PUT
questions.explanation: PUT is idempotent (calling it multiple times with the same data produces the same result) and replaces the entire resource at the specified URL. PATCH performs a partial update; POST is not idempotent and creates new resources.

questions.statement: In web development, what is Progressive Enhancement?
questions.option_a: Building separate mobile and desktop versions of a website for different audiences
questions.option_b: Gradually loading page content as the user scrolls down the page
questions.option_c: Starting with a functional base experience for all browsers and adding advanced features for more capable browsers
questions.option_d: Progressively reducing page complexity based on connection speed
questions.explanation: Progressive Enhancement is a design strategy that starts by building a core experience that works on all browsers, then layering enhanced functionality and styling for browsers that support more advanced features, ensuring broad accessibility.

questions.statement: A developer wants to implement real-time bidirectional communication between a browser client and a server, such as for a live chat application. Which technology is most appropriate?
questions.option_a: Long Polling
questions.option_b: Server-Sent Events
questions.option_c: WebSockets
questions.option_d: Regular HTTP Polling
questions.explanation: WebSockets provide a persistent, full-duplex communication channel over a single TCP connection, enabling real-time bidirectional data transfer. Server-Sent Events only support server-to-client unidirectional streaming. Long polling and regular polling are HTTP workarounds with higher overhead.

questions.statement: What does 'minification' of JavaScript and CSS files achieve in web performance optimization?
questions.option_a: It reduces the logical complexity of the code by removing redundant algorithms
questions.option_b: It removes whitespace, comments, and shortens variable names to reduce file size without changing functionality
questions.option_c: It converts ES6+ syntax to ES5 for browser compatibility
questions.option_d: It splits large files into smaller chunks for parallel downloading
questions.explanation: Minification removes all unnecessary characters (whitespace, comments, long variable names) from source code without changing its behavior, reducing file size and therefore download time. Transpilation converts syntax; code splitting divides files.

questions.statement: Which CSS property is used to make an element's position fixed relative to the viewport, so it stays in place when the user scrolls?
questions.option_a: position: absolute
questions.option_b: position: sticky
questions.option_c: position: relative
questions.option_d: position: fixed
questions.explanation: position:fixed removes an element from the document flow and positions it relative to the viewport, so it remains in the same position on screen as the user scrolls. position:sticky is a hybrid that switches between relative and fixed.

questions.statement: A developer writes a JavaScript function that returns a function with access to a private counter variable. External code can only increment or read the counter using the returned function's methods. What design principle does this implement?
questions.option_a: Inheritance
questions.option_b: Polymorphism
questions.option_c: The Module Pattern using Closures
questions.option_d: The Prototype Pattern
questions.explanation: The Module Pattern uses closures to encapsulate private state (the counter variable) that cannot be directly accessed from outside the function. The returned object exposes only public methods, mimicking private/public encapsulation.

questions.statement: What is the purpose of the package-lock.json file in a Node.js project?
questions.option_a: To define which npm scripts can be run in the project
questions.option_b: To lock the exact version of every installed dependency and its transitive dependencies
questions.option_c: To list all Node.js version compatibility requirements for the project
questions.option_d: To store the project's environment variables for local development
questions.explanation: package-lock.json records the exact resolved version of every package in the dependency tree, ensuring that npm install produces an identical dependency tree on every machine. This prevents 'works on my machine' issues caused by version drift.

questions.statement: Which React pattern involves a component that renders its children with additional props or state, without adding DOM elements?
questions.option_a: Higher-Order Component (HOC)
questions.option_b: Render Props
questions.option_c: Context API
questions.option_d: Compound Components
questions.explanation: A Higher-Order Component (HOC) is a function that takes a component and returns a new component with enhanced or additional props and behavior. The Render Props pattern passes rendering logic as a function prop; both solve prop sharing but differently.

questions.statement: What does the acronym WCAG stand for in web accessibility?
questions.option_a: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines
questions.option_b: Web Compatibility and Authoring Guide
questions.option_c: World Content Accessibility Goals
questions.option_d: Web Component Accessibility Guidelines
questions.explanation: WCAG stands for Web Content Accessibility Guidelines, published by the W3C, which define standards for making web content accessible to people with disabilities. The current major version is WCAG 2.1. The other options are fabricated expansions.

questions.statement: A developer observes that their web server logs show thousands of requests per second from the same IP address to a login endpoint. Which security measure would most directly mitigate this brute-force attack?
questions.option_a: Adding HTTPS to the login endpoint
questions.option_b: Implementing rate limiting on the login endpoint
questions.option_c: Switching from POST to GET for the login form
questions.option_d: Using localStorage to store the session token
questions.explanation: Rate limiting restricts the number of requests a client can make to an endpoint within a given time window, directly preventing brute-force attacks that rely on making many rapid attempts. HTTPS encrypts traffic but does not limit request frequency.

questions.statement: What is a 'web manifest' file in the context of Progressive Web Applications (PWAs)?
questions.option_a: A configuration file that lists all JavaScript dependencies for the application
questions.option_b: A JSON file that provides information about the app (name, icons, start URL) to enable installation on a device's home screen
questions.option_c: A security policy file that defines which origins can access the application's resources
questions.option_d: A deployment script that automates the process of publishing the application to a web server
questions.explanation: The Web App Manifest is a JSON file that tells the browser about a Progressive Web App and how it should behave when installed, including its name, icons, theme colors, and start URL, enabling add-to-home-screen functionality.

questions.statement: Which CSS selector targets the first child element of its parent, regardless of element type?
questions.option_a: element:first-of-type
questions.option_b: element:nth-child(1)
questions.option_c: element:first-child
questions.option_d: * :first-child
questions.explanation: The :first-child pseudo-class selects an element that is the first child of its parent, regardless of element type. :first-of-type selects the first element of a specific type among its siblings.

questions.statement: A backend developer creates an API endpoint /api/users/123 that returns user data. According to REST principles, which HTTP method should be used to retrieve this resource?
questions.option_a: POST
questions.option_b: PUT
questions.option_c: DELETE
questions.option_d: GET
questions.explanation: GET is the correct RESTful HTTP method for retrieving a resource. REST principles define GET as safe and idempotent, used exclusively for data retrieval without side effects. POST, PUT, and DELETE modify server state.

questions.statement: What is the difference between a cookie and a session in web development?
questions.option_a: A cookie is server-side storage; a session is client-side storage
questions.option_b: A cookie is stored on the client; a session is stored on the server, typically referenced by a cookie containing the session ID
questions.option_c: A cookie expires when the browser closes; a session persists indefinitely
questions.option_d: A cookie holds only strings; a session can hold complex JavaScript objects
questions.explanation: A cookie is a small file stored in the user's browser. A session stores user data on the server and uses a session ID (often stored in a cookie) to associate server-side data with specific clients. The session itself is server-side.

questions.statement: Which frontend build tool is known for its extremely fast development server using native ES modules, avoiding the need to bundle code during development?
questions.option_a: Webpack
questions.option_b: Parcel
questions.option_c: Grunt
questions.option_d: Vite
questions.explanation: Vite leverages native browser ES module support to serve source files directly during development without bundling, resulting in near-instant server start and fast hot module replacement. Webpack must bundle the entire application first.

questions.statement: A developer needs to store relational data with complex queries and relationships for a web application, such as user orders with multiple products. Which type of database is most appropriate?
questions.option_a: Document Database (e.g., MongoDB)
questions.option_b: Key-Value Store (e.g., Redis)
questions.option_c: Graph Database (e.g., Neo4j)
questions.option_d: Relational Database (e.g., PostgreSQL)
questions.explanation: Relational databases like PostgreSQL are designed for structured data with well-defined relationships, supporting complex JOIN queries needed for relational scenarios like orders with products. Document stores are better for hierarchical, schema-flexible data.

questions.statement: What is the purpose of using a linter like ESLint in a JavaScript project?
questions.option_a: To bundle JavaScript files into a single output file for production
questions.option_b: To statically analyze JavaScript code for potential errors, bugs, and style inconsistencies
questions.option_c: To transpile modern JavaScript syntax into browser-compatible ES5 code
questions.option_d: To run automated unit tests and report code coverage
questions.explanation: ESLint is a static analysis tool (linter) that examines JavaScript source code without running it, identifying potential errors, enforcing coding standards, and flagging style inconsistencies based on a configurable set of rules.

questions.statement: Which CSS technique is used to make text overflow with an ellipsis (...) when it exceeds its container width?
questions.option_a: overflow: ellipsis; width: 100%;
questions.option_b: white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis;
questions.option_c: text-decoration: truncate; max-width: 100%;
questions.option_d: display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 1;
questions.explanation: The combination of white-space:nowrap (prevents wrapping), overflow:hidden (hides overflow), and text-overflow:ellipsis (adds '...') achieves single-line text truncation with an ellipsis in CSS.

questions.statement: In web security, what is a 'session fixation' attack?
questions.option_a: An attack where the attacker steals an active session cookie using XSS
questions.option_b: An attack where the attacker sets a known session ID before login, then hijacks the session after the victim authenticates
questions.option_c: An attack where the attacker fixes the server's session timeout to keep a session alive indefinitely
questions.option_d: An attack where the attacker replays old session tokens to gain unauthorized access
questions.explanation: In session fixation, the attacker sets a predetermined session ID before the victim logs in, then uses that same known ID after authentication. The defense is to always issue a new session ID after successful login.

questions.statement: What is the primary advantage of using a CSS preprocessor like SASS over plain CSS?
questions.option_a: It automatically adds vendor prefixes to CSS properties for browser compatibility
questions.option_b: It allows writing CSS with variables, nesting, mixins, and functions that compile to standard CSS
questions.option_c: It serves CSS files faster by compressing them in memory at runtime
questions.option_d: It enforces a strict naming convention that prevents CSS selector conflicts
questions.explanation: SASS extends CSS with features like variables, nesting, mixins, and functions that make stylesheets more maintainable. SASS files are compiled into standard CSS. Autoprefixer (separate tool) adds vendor prefixes; SASS is a preprocessor.

questions.statement: A developer needs to check if an array contains a specific value in JavaScript. Which method returns a boolean indicating whether the value is present?
questions.option_a: array.find()
questions.option_b: array.indexOf()
questions.option_c: array.includes()
questions.option_d: array.some()
questions.explanation: array.includes() directly returns a boolean (true/false) indicating whether the specified value exists in the array. find() returns the element or undefined; indexOf() returns the index or -1; some() takes a function and checks a condition.

questions.statement: What does the acronym CDN stand for in web development?
questions.option_a: Content Distribution Node
questions.option_b: Content Delivery Network
questions.option_c: Centralized Data Network
questions.option_d: Client Deployment Namespace
questions.explanation: CDN stands for Content Delivery Network, a geographically distributed group of servers that cache and deliver web content (images, CSS, JS) from locations closer to users to reduce latency. The other options are fabricated expansions.

questions.statement: Which HTTP response header is used to specify how long a browser should cache a resource before making a new request?
questions.option_a: ETag
questions.option_b: Last-Modified
questions.option_c: Cache-Control
questions.option_d: Pragma
questions.explanation: The Cache-Control header is the primary, modern mechanism for defining caching policies (e.g., max-age=3600 caches the resource for one hour). ETag and Last-Modified are used for conditional request validation, not initial cache duration.

questions.statement: In the context of web development, what does 'hydration' mean in server-side rendering frameworks?
questions.option_a: Downloading water-themed CSS themes for a page template
questions.option_b: The process where the browser's JavaScript attaches event listeners to server-rendered HTML, making it interactive
questions.option_c: The process of pre-fetching data from the server before the user navigates to a page
questions.option_d: Automatically converting CSS color names to hexadecimal values
questions.explanation: Hydration is the process by which a client-side JavaScript framework (like Next.js or Nuxt) takes over the static HTML rendered by the server and attaches event listeners and state, making the page fully interactive.

questions.statement: A developer uses Docker to containerize their web application. What is the primary benefit of containerization for web deployment?
questions.option_a: It automatically scales the application to handle more users
questions.option_b: It ensures the application runs consistently across different environments by packaging the app and its dependencies together
questions.option_c: It encrypts all network communication between the application and its clients
questions.option_d: It provides a built-in database management system for the application
questions.explanation: Docker containers package an application with all its dependencies (runtime, libraries, config files), ensuring it runs identically across development, staging, and production environments, eliminating environment-specific bugs.

questions.statement: Which JavaScript array method creates a new array by applying a transformation function to every element of the original array?
questions.option_a: filter()
questions.option_b: reduce()
questions.option_c: forEach()
questions.option_d: map()
questions.explanation: map() creates a new array by calling a provided function on every element of the calling array and returning the result. forEach() iterates over elements but returns undefined; filter() returns a subset; reduce() aggregates.

questions.statement: What is the purpose of an API gateway in a microservices-based web architecture?
questions.option_a: To serve as the primary database connection pool for all microservices
questions.option_b: To provide a single entry point for all client requests, handling routing, authentication, and rate limiting
questions.option_c: To act as a message broker for asynchronous communication between services
questions.option_d: To monitor the health and uptime of all individual microservices
questions.explanation: An API Gateway is a server that acts as the single entry point for all client requests, routing them to appropriate backend microservices while handling cross-cutting concerns like authentication, authorization, rate limiting, and logging.

questions.statement: Which technique in CSS allows you to apply styles to an element based on its position relative to the viewport during scrolling, using CSS alone?
questions.option_a: CSS Intersection Observer
questions.option_b: CSS scroll-snap
questions.option_c: CSS position:sticky
questions.option_d: CSS @scroll-timeline
questions.explanation: position:sticky is a CSS-only technique that makes an element behave like position:relative until it reaches a specified scroll threshold, then behaves like position:fixed. This is commonly used for sticky navigation bars without JavaScript.

questions.statement: What is the purpose of a 'sitemap.xml' file in web development?
questions.option_a: To define the folder structure of the web application's source code
questions.option_b: To help search engines discover and index all pages of a website efficiently
questions.option_c: To map API endpoint URLs to their corresponding backend controller functions
