questions.option_d: To list all CSS files used by the website for browser preloading
questions.explanation: A sitemap.xml file lists all important URLs of a website and provides metadata (update frequency, priority) to help search engines like Google discover and crawl the site's content more efficiently.

questions.statement: A developer implements OAuth 2.0 to allow users to log in with their Google account. What is the role of the 'authorization code' in this flow?
questions.option_a: It is the final access token used to make API calls on behalf of the user
questions.option_b: It is a temporary, single-use code exchanged server-side for an access token, preventing the token from being exposed in the browser URL
questions.option_c: It is the client's secret key used to authenticate the application to Google
questions.option_d: It is a long-lived token used to obtain new access tokens without re-authentication
questions.explanation: In the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code Flow, the authorization code is a short-lived, one-time-use code that the client server exchanges for an access token via a back-channel server-to-server request. This prevents the access token from appearing in browser history or URLs.

questions.statement: Which HTML attribute can be added to a form input to trigger native browser-side validation with a specific regex pattern?
questions.option_a: validate
questions.option_b: constraint
questions.option_c: pattern
questions.option_d: regex
questions.explanation: The pattern attribute on an HTML input accepts a regular expression. The browser validates the input's value against this pattern before form submission and shows a validation message if it does not match.

questions.statement: What is the 'box model' in CSS?
questions.option_a: A layout system for arranging flex items in rows and columns
questions.option_b: The set of rules governing how web servers package HTTP responses
questions.option_c: The conceptual structure of every HTML element, comprising content, padding, border, and margin
questions.option_d: A JavaScript pattern for encapsulating DOM manipulation logic
questions.explanation: The CSS box model describes how every HTML element is rendered as a rectangular box with four areas: the content area, padding (inside the border), border, and margin (outside the border). Understanding it is fundamental to CSS layout.

questions.statement: A developer needs to run a piece of code after all promises in an async waterfall have resolved. Which async/await pattern correctly handles errors in each step?
questions.option_a: Wrapping each await in a separate if-else block
questions.option_b: Using try-catch blocks around await expressions to handle rejections
questions.option_c: Chaining .then() and .catch() on each await call
questions.option_d: Using Promise.resolve() before each await to prevent rejections
questions.explanation: Wrapping await expressions inside try-catch blocks is the correct pattern to handle promise rejections in async/await code. Without try-catch, an unhandled rejection in an await expression will propagate as an unhandled exception.

questions.statement: What is 'event delegation' in JavaScript DOM manipulation?
questions.option_a: Delegating event handling to a server-side script instead of the browser
questions.option_b: Attaching a single event listener to a parent element to handle events from multiple child elements
questions.option_c: Assigning multiple event handlers to a single DOM element
questions.option_d: Removing event listeners from elements that are not currently visible
questions.explanation: Event delegation exploits event bubbling by attaching one listener to a parent element that intercepts events from its children. This is more efficient than attaching separate listeners to each child, especially for dynamically created elements.

questions.statement: Which backend Node.js framework is most commonly used to build RESTful APIs with minimal configuration?
questions.option_a: Django
questions.option_b: Laravel
questions.option_c: Express.js
questions.option_d: Spring Boot
questions.explanation: Express.js is the most popular, minimal, and flexible Node.js web application framework for building RESTful APIs. Django is Python-based; Laravel is PHP-based; Spring Boot is Java-based.

questions.statement: What is the correct way to include an external JavaScript file in an HTML document for deferred loading?
questions.option_a: <script href='app.js' defer></script>
questions.option_b: <link rel='script' href='app.js'>
questions.option_c: <script src='app.js' defer></script>
questions.option_d: <script type='module' href='app.js'>
questions.explanation: <script src='app.js' defer> is the correct syntax. The src attribute specifies the file path, and defer loads the script asynchronously and executes it after HTML parsing is complete. The href attribute is for <link> tags, not <script> tags.

questions.statement: A user reports that their shopping cart items disappear when they close the browser tab. The developer stored cart items in sessionStorage. Which storage type should replace it to persist across sessions?
questions.option_a: IndexedDB only
questions.option_b: Cookies with HttpOnly flag
questions.option_c: localStorage
questions.option_d: A server-side database session
questions.explanation: localStorage persists data across browser sessions (until explicitly cleared), making it suitable for storing shopping cart items that should survive tab or browser closure. sessionStorage is cleared when the tab is closed.

questions.statement: In CSS, what does the 'cascade' in Cascading Style Sheets refer to?
questions.option_a: The animation of elements flowing down the page on scroll
questions.option_b: The hierarchical process of determining which CSS rules apply when multiple rules target the same element
questions.option_c: The inheritance of styles from parent elements to child elements
questions.option_d: The sequential loading of multiple CSS files in the order they are linked
questions.explanation: The cascade is the algorithm CSS uses to determine which style declarations win when multiple conflicting rules apply to the same element, considering specificity, origin, and source order. Inheritance is a related but separate concept.

questions.statement: Which web development tool continuously watches source files for changes and automatically rebuilds or reloads the browser without manual intervention?
questions.option_a: A code linter
questions.option_b: A hot module replacement (HMR) dev server
questions.option_c: A static site generator
questions.option_d: A version control pre-commit hook
questions.explanation: Hot Module Replacement (HMR), provided by dev servers like Webpack Dev Server or Vite, watches for file changes and injects the updated module directly into the running application without a full browser reload, preserving application state.

questions.statement: What is the purpose of the HTTP OPTIONS method in the context of CORS?
questions.option_a: To retrieve the headers of a resource without its body
questions.option_b: To list the available HTTP methods for a resource
questions.option_c: To send a preflight request to check whether the actual cross-origin request is safe to send
questions.option_d: To update resource metadata without changing its content
questions.explanation: In CORS, browsers automatically send an HTTP OPTIONS preflight request before certain cross-origin requests to check that the server permits the actual request method and headers. The server responds with allowed origins, methods, and headers.

questions.statement: A developer uses the CSS property 'display: none' to hide an element. How does this differ from 'visibility: hidden'?
questions.option_a: Both have identical effects on layout and accessibility
questions.option_b: display:none keeps the element in the layout while making it invisible; visibility:hidden removes it from the layout
questions.option_c: display:none removes the element from the document flow entirely; visibility:hidden makes it invisible but preserves its layout space
questions.option_d: display:none is only supported in modern browsers; visibility:hidden has broader support
questions.explanation: display:none removes the element from the document flow, so it takes up no space. visibility:hidden makes the element invisible but it still occupies its layout space. Both hide the element from the accessibility tree.

questions.statement: Which technique allows a web application to request resources from a different origin using cookies and credentials?
questions.option_a: Including 'mode: no-cors' in the fetch() options
questions.option_b: Setting withCredentials: true and ensuring the server responds with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
questions.option_c: Disabling the Content-Security-Policy header in the request
questions.option_d: Setting the cookie's SameSite attribute to 'None' in the frontend JavaScript
questions.explanation: To include credentials (cookies, authorization headers) in cross-origin requests, the client must set credentials:'include' (fetch) or withCredentials:true (XHR), AND the server must respond with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials:true and a specific (not wildcard) origin.

questions.statement: What does 'SEO' stand for, and what is its primary goal in web development?
questions.option_a: Site Enhancement Operations; improving server response time
questions.option_b: Search Engine Optimization; improving a website's visibility and ranking in organic search results
questions.option_c: Secure Element Operations; encrypting web communications
questions.option_d: Site Experience Optimization; improving user interface design
questions.explanation: SEO stands for Search Engine Optimization, the practice of improving a website's technical setup, content, and authority to increase its organic (unpaid) visibility in search engine results pages. The other options are fabricated expansions.

questions.statement: A full-stack developer needs to define a schema for a MongoDB collection in their Node.js application to enforce data structure and validation. Which library is most commonly used for this?
questions.option_a: Sequelize
questions.option_b: TypeORM
questions.option_c: Mongoose
questions.option_d: Knex.js
questions.explanation: Mongoose is the most popular ODM (Object Data Modeling) library for MongoDB and Node.js, providing schema definition, data validation, middleware, and query building. Sequelize and TypeORM are ORMs for relational SQL databases.

questions.statement: Which JavaScript feature allows developers to destructure an array, extracting specific elements by their position into named variables in a single statement?
questions.option_a: Array Spread Operator
questions.option_b: Array Destructuring Assignment
questions.option_c: Array Mapping
questions.option_d: Object Destructuring
questions.explanation: Array Destructuring Assignment allows extracting elements by position into named variables in a single expression, e.g., const [first, second] = myArray. Object destructuring works the same way but for object properties by key name.

questions.statement: What is the primary purpose of using HTTPS during web application authentication?
questions.option_a: To validate that the web server's IP address matches its domain name
questions.option_b: To encrypt credentials and session tokens in transit, preventing interception by attackers
questions.option_c: To authenticate the identity of the user's device to the server
questions.option_d: To prevent multiple concurrent login sessions from the same user
questions.explanation: HTTPS (TLS) encrypts data transmitted between the client and server, protecting credentials (usernames and passwords) and session tokens from being intercepted by an attacker performing a network eavesdropping attack.

questions.statement: A developer wants to preload a critical font file to prevent layout shifts caused by font loading. Which HTML tag and attribute combination is correct?
questions.option_a: <link rel='stylesheet' href='font.woff2'>
questions.option_b: <link rel='preload' href='font.woff2' as='font' type='font/woff2' crossorigin>
questions.option_c: <script src='font.woff2' async></script>
questions.option_d: <meta name='preload' content='font.woff2'>
questions.explanation: The correct syntax for preloading a font is <link rel='preload' href='font.woff2' as='font' type='font/woff2' crossorigin>. The as='font' attribute is required so the browser applies the correct priority, and crossorigin is required even for same-origin fonts.

questions.statement: Which of the following HTTP response headers helps browsers defend against MIME type sniffing attacks?
questions.option_a: Access-Control-Allow-Origin
questions.option_b: Content-Security-Policy
questions.option_c: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
questions.option_d: Referrer-Policy
questions.explanation: The X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff header prevents browsers from MIME-sniffing a response away from the declared Content-Type, stopping attacks that exploit browser guess-work about file types to execute malicious scripts.

questions.statement: In RESTful API design, what is the correct URL structure for retrieving a single resource with ID 42 from a 'products' collection?
questions.option_a: GET /getProduct?id=42
questions.option_b: GET /products/42
questions.option_c: POST /products/find/42
questions.option_d: GET /product/get/42
questions.explanation: RESTful URL design uses nouns to represent resources. GET /products/42 correctly identifies a specific product resource by its ID within the products collection. Verbs like 'get', 'find' in URLs violate REST conventions.

questions.statement: What is the purpose of the JavaScript 'spread operator' (...) when used with an array?
questions.option_a: It converts an array into a comma-separated string
questions.option_b: It expands an array's elements into individual arguments or elements
questions.option_c: It creates a deep copy of all nested objects within an array
questions.option_d: It filters out undefined and null values from an array
questions.explanation: The spread operator (...) expands an iterable (like an array) into individual elements, useful for combining arrays, passing array elements as function arguments, or creating shallow copies of arrays.

questions.statement: Which web performance metric measures the time from navigation start to when the largest visible content element in the viewport has rendered?
questions.option_a: First Contentful Paint (FCP)
questions.option_b: Time to Interactive (TTI)
questions.option_c: Largest Contentful Paint (LCP)
questions.option_d: Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS)
questions.explanation: Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) measures when the largest visible content element (image or text block) has rendered, representing the page's perceived load speed for the main content. FCP measures when any content first appears.

questions.statement: A developer is building a multi-page form with complex state. After navigating between form steps, the data resets. The developer is using React with functional components. What is the best solution for persisting form state across steps?
questions.option_a: Using CSS display:none to hide previous steps instead of navigating away
questions.option_b: Lifting form state up to a common parent component or using a state management library
questions.option_c: Storing form data in the URL query parameters after each step
questions.option_d: Using document.getElementById to read values from hidden form fields
questions.explanation: Lifting state to a common parent component that wraps all steps ensures the data persists across step navigation. Using Redux or Context API is another valid solution. CSS hiding is impractical for complex forms with many fields.

questions.statement: What is the difference between a 200 OK and 204 No Content HTTP response?
questions.option_a: 200 always includes a response body; 204 indicates the server is unavailable
questions.option_b: 200 indicates a successful request with a response body; 204 indicates success with intentionally no response body
questions.option_c: 200 is used for GET requests only; 204 is used for POST requests
questions.option_d: 200 indicates cached content; 204 indicates freshly retrieved content
questions.explanation: 200 OK indicates a successful request and includes a response body with the requested data. 204 No Content indicates success but intentionally provides no response body, commonly used for DELETE or PUT operations.

questions.statement: Which property of the Fetch API's Response object should a developer check to confirm the HTTP request succeeded before processing the response body?
questions.option_a: response.status === 200
questions.option_b: response.type === 'basic'
questions.option_c: response.ok
questions.option_d: response.redirected === false
questions.explanation: response.ok is a boolean property that returns true when the HTTP status code is in the range 200-299 (successful), providing a simple way to check for success before attempting to parse the response body.

questions.statement: A web application needs to send real-time stock price updates from the server to all connected clients. The data flows only from server to client. Which technology is most efficient for this scenario?
questions.option_a: WebSockets
questions.option_b: Long Polling
questions.option_c: HTTP Streaming with Server-Sent Events
questions.option_d: AJAX Interval Polling
questions.explanation: Server-Sent Events (SSE) are designed for unidirectional, server-to-client streaming over a standard HTTP connection, making them perfect for stock ticker updates. WebSockets support bidirectional communication, which is more complex than needed here.

questions.statement: What does the CSS property 'overflow: hidden' do when applied to a container element?
questions.option_a: It hides the container from screen readers and assistive technologies
questions.option_b: It clips any content that extends beyond the container's boundaries so the overflow is not visible
questions.option_c: It prevents the user from scrolling within the element if content overflows
questions.option_d: It automatically reduces the font size of content to fit within the container
questions.explanation: overflow:hidden clips any content that extends beyond the element's padding box, making overflowing content invisible. overflow:auto or overflow:scroll would add scrollbars; neither option affects assistive technology visibility.

questions.statement: In the context of web APIs, what does 'idempotency' mean for an HTTP method?
questions.option_a: The method can be called without authentication
questions.option_b: Making multiple identical requests produces the same result as a single request
questions.option_c: The method's response is always cached by the browser
questions.option_d: The method transfers data in an encrypted format
questions.explanation: An idempotent HTTP method produces the same server state regardless of how many times it is called with the same input. GET, PUT, and DELETE are idempotent; POST is not, because multiple POST requests create multiple resources.

questions.statement: Which of the following is a key advantage of using TypeScript over plain JavaScript for large web applications?
questions.option_a: TypeScript runs faster than JavaScript in all browser environments
questions.option_b: TypeScript provides static type checking that catches type-related errors before runtime
questions.option_c: TypeScript eliminates the need for unit testing by enforcing correctness at compile time
questions.option_d: TypeScript is natively supported by all browsers without a transpilation step
questions.explanation: TypeScript's static type system catches type-related errors at compile time (during development), before the code is run, significantly reducing runtime errors in large codebases. TypeScript must be transpiled to JavaScript; it does not run natively in browsers.

questions.statement: A developer adds the following to their .gitignore file: node_modules/. What is the purpose of this entry?
questions.option_a: It prevents the node_modules directory from being deleted when running npm uninstall
questions.option_b: It excludes the node_modules directory from being tracked and committed to the Git repository
questions.option_c: It tells webpack to ignore all files inside node_modules during bundling
questions.option_d: It prevents npm from installing packages inside the node_modules directory
questions.explanation: Adding node_modules/ to .gitignore prevents this directory (containing all installed dependencies) from being committed to the repository, since it can be regenerated from package.json using npm install and is typically very large.

questions.statement: What is the primary role of the 'Content-Security-Policy' (CSP) HTTP header in web security?
questions.option_a: To enforce HTTPS for all resources loaded on the page
questions.option_b: To define which sources of content the browser is allowed to load, mitigating XSS and injection attacks
questions.option_c: To prevent the browser from caching sensitive API responses
questions.option_d: To restrict which HTTP methods clients can use when calling the server
questions.explanation: CSP allows web servers to declare approved sources of scripts, styles, images, and other resources. By restricting which origins can load content, CSP significantly reduces the risk of XSS attacks by blocking unauthorized script execution.

questions.statement: Which JavaScript method is used to convert a JavaScript object into a JSON-formatted string for transmission or storage?
questions.option_a: JSON.parse()
questions.option_b: JSON.decode()
questions.option_c: JSON.stringify()
questions.option_d: JSON.serialize()
questions.explanation: JSON.stringify() converts a JavaScript object or value into a JSON string. JSON.parse() does the reverse, converting a JSON string back into a JavaScript object. JSON.decode() and JSON.serialize() are not standard JavaScript methods.

questions.statement: In Node.js, what is the primary purpose of the 'middleware' concept in Express.js?
questions.option_a: To serve as an intermediary layer between the database and the API routes
questions.option_b: Functions that execute during the request-response cycle with access to req, res, and next for cross-cutting concerns
questions.option_c: To define the URL routing structure of the application
questions.option_d: To manage package dependencies and version compatibility
questions.explanation: Middleware in Express.js are functions that have access to the request (req), response (res), and the next middleware function, used for cross-cutting concerns like authentication, logging, and error handling that apply across multiple routes.

questions.statement: What is the main purpose of 'database indexing' in web applications?
questions.option_a: To encrypt database records for security compliance
questions.option_b: To speed up data retrieval operations at the cost of additional write and storage overhead
questions.option_c: To normalize database tables to eliminate data redundancy
questions.option_d: To create relationships between tables using foreign keys
questions.explanation: Database indexes create optimized data structures that allow the database engine to find rows matching query conditions much faster than scanning every row, significantly improving read query performance at the expense of additional storage and slower writes.

questions.statement: What does the acronym JWT stand for in web authentication?
questions.option_a: JavaScript Web Token
questions.option_b: JSON Web Transfer
questions.option_c: JSON Web Token
questions.option_d: Java Web Token
questions.explanation: JWT stands for JSON Web Token, a compact, URL-safe token format used for securely transmitting information as a JSON object. JWTs are commonly used for stateless authentication. The other options are fabricated expansions.

questions.statement: What does AI stand for in the context of computer science?
questions.option_a: Automated Intelligence
questions.option_b: Artificial Intelligence
questions.option_c: Analytical Integration
questions.option_d: Augmented Instruction
questions.explanation: AI stands for Artificial Intelligence, the field of computer science dedicated to creating systems capable of performing tasks that typically require human intelligence. The other options are fabricated expansions.

questions.statement: A machine learning model performs well on the training data but very poorly on unseen test data. Which problem does this describe?
questions.option_a: Underfitting
questions.option_b: Bias
questions.option_c: Overfitting
questions.option_d: Data leakage
questions.explanation: Overfitting occurs when a model learns the training data too well—including its noise and irrelevant patterns—and fails to generalize to new data. Underfitting is the opposite: the model fails to capture the underlying pattern even in training data.

questions.statement: Which Python library provides the DataFrame data structure and is essential for data manipulation and analysis?
questions.option_a: NumPy
questions.option_b: Matplotlib
questions.option_c: Scikit-learn
questions.option_d: Pandas
questions.explanation: Pandas provides the DataFrame structure for tabular data manipulation, including reading, cleaning, filtering, and aggregating data. NumPy handles numerical arrays; Matplotlib is for visualization; Scikit-learn is for machine learning.

questions.statement: In supervised learning, what is the primary role of the 'label' in a training dataset?
questions.option_a: To describe the input features used by the model
questions.option_b: To provide the correct output the model should learn to predict
questions.option_c: To define the hyperparameters of the learning algorithm
questions.option_d: To specify the loss function used during training
questions.explanation: In supervised learning, a label is the ground-truth output value associated with each training example. The model learns to map input features to these labels by minimizing the error between its predictions and the true labels.

questions.statement: A data scientist is exploring a new dataset and creates histograms, box plots, and correlation matrices before building any model. What phase of the data science process are they performing?
questions.option_a: Feature Engineering
questions.option_b: Model Evaluation
questions.option_c: Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)
questions.option_d: Data Pre-processing
questions.explanation: Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) is the process of visually and statistically examining a dataset to understand distributions, relationships, outliers, and patterns before formal modeling. It informs subsequent feature engineering and model selection.

questions.statement: What does the acronym ML stand for in data science?
questions.option_a: Multi-Layer Learning
questions.option_b: Machine Linguistics
questions.option_c: Machine Learning
questions.option_d: Mathematical Logic
questions.explanation: ML stands for Machine Learning, a subset of AI where systems learn to perform tasks by finding patterns in data without being explicitly programmed with rules. The other options are fabricated expansions.

questions.statement: Which type of machine learning algorithm learns from a dataset that has no labeled output, attempting to find hidden structure in the data?
questions.option_a: Supervised Learning
questions.option_b: Reinforcement Learning
questions.option_c: Transfer Learning
questions.option_d: Unsupervised Learning
questions.explanation: Unsupervised Learning algorithms find patterns, groupings, or structures in unlabeled data. Examples include clustering and dimensionality reduction. Supervised learning requires labeled training examples.

questions.statement: A machine learning model has high bias and high variance. After adding more training data, the model improves slightly but still performs poorly. What does this most likely indicate?
questions.option_a: The model is overfitting and needs regularization
questions.option_b: The model is too simple and underfitting the data
questions.option_c: The dataset has too many duplicate records
questions.option_d: The learning rate is set too high
questions.explanation: High bias indicates that the model is too simple to capture the underlying patterns (underfitting). Adding more data does not fix underfitting—a more complex model, better features, or reduced regularization is needed.

questions.statement: Which mathematical concept measures the average squared difference between predicted and actual values, serving as a common regression loss function?
questions.option_a: Mean Absolute Error (MAE)
questions.option_b: Cross-Entropy Loss
questions.option_c: Mean Squared Error (MSE)
questions.option_d: R-squared
questions.explanation: Mean Squared Error (MSE) calculates the average of the squared differences between predictions and actual values. Squaring penalizes larger errors more heavily than MAE. Cross-Entropy Loss is used for classification, not regression.

questions.statement: In the context of neural networks, which activation function outputs values between 0 and 1 and is commonly used in binary classification output layers?
questions.option_a: ReLU (Rectified Linear Unit)
questions.option_b: Tanh
questions.option_c: Leaky ReLU
questions.option_d: Sigmoid
questions.explanation: The Sigmoid function maps any real-valued input to a value between 0 and 1, making it suitable for binary classification output layers where the output represents a probability. ReLU outputs values from 0 to infinity.

questions.statement: A data analyst discovers that 30% of values in a numerical column are missing. Which imputation method is most robust for skewed distributions?
questions.option_a: Delete all rows containing missing values
questions.option_b: Replace missing values with the column mean
questions.option_c: Replace missing values with the column median
questions.option_d: Replace missing values with zero
questions.explanation: For skewed distributions, the median is more robust than the mean because it is not affected by extreme outliers. Mean imputation can distort the distribution in skewed data. Deleting 30% of rows causes significant data loss.

questions.statement: What does the acronym KNN stand for in machine learning?
questions.option_a: Kernel Node Network
questions.option_b: K-Nearest Nodes
questions.option_c: K-Nearest Neighbors
questions.option_d: Kernel Neural Network
questions.explanation: KNN stands for K-Nearest Neighbors, a simple, instance-based classification or regression algorithm that assigns labels based on the majority class (or average value) of the K nearest training examples. The other options are fabricated.

questions.statement: In the k-means clustering algorithm, what does 'k' represent?
questions.option_a: The number of features used to train the model
questions.option_b: The number of iterations the algorithm runs before convergence
questions.option_c: The number of clusters the algorithm will form in the data
questions.option_d: The maximum distance allowed between two data points in the same cluster
questions.explanation: In k-means, 'k' is a user-specified hyperparameter that defines the number of clusters the algorithm will partition the data into. The algorithm assigns each data point to the nearest centroid among k centroids.

questions.statement: A random forest model outperforms a single decision tree on the same dataset. Which ensemble learning concept explains this improvement?
questions.option_a: Boosting reduces the bias of each weak learner
questions.option_b: Combining multiple diverse models reduces variance through averaging
questions.option_c: Bagging increases the depth of each individual tree
questions.option_d: Stacking uses a meta-learner to combine predictions from homogeneous models
questions.explanation: Random Forest is a bagging ensemble that trains multiple decision trees on random data subsets and combines their predictions by averaging or voting, reducing variance and improving generalization compared to any single tree.

questions.statement: Which Python library is primarily used for creating static, animated, and interactive visualizations in data analytics?
questions.option_a: Pandas
questions.option_b: TensorFlow
questions.option_c: Scikit-learn
questions.option_d: Matplotlib
questions.explanation: Matplotlib is the foundational Python library for creating 2D plots and charts such as histograms, scatter plots, and line charts. Seaborn builds on Matplotlib for statistical visualization; Pandas uses Matplotlib internally for basic plots.

questions.statement: What is the purpose of the train-test split in a machine learning workflow?
questions.option_a: To duplicate the dataset for robustness testing
questions.option_b: To evaluate the model's performance on data it has not seen during training
questions.option_c: To increase the total amount of training data available
questions.option_d: To balance the class distribution within the training set
questions.explanation: Splitting data into training and test sets allows a model to be trained on one portion and evaluated on a completely separate, unseen portion, providing an unbiased estimate of how the model will perform on new real-world data.

questions.statement: In deep learning, what is the role of the backpropagation algorithm?
questions.option_a: To initialize the weights of a neural network randomly before training
questions.option_b: To compute gradients of the loss with respect to each weight and propagate them backward for weight updates
questions.option_c: To select the optimal architecture of a neural network automatically
questions.option_d: To normalize the input data before feeding it into the network
questions.explanation: Backpropagation applies the chain rule of calculus to compute the gradient of the loss function with respect to each weight in the network, enabling gradient descent to update the weights and minimize the loss.

questions.statement: A data scientist wants to reduce the number of features in a dataset to two dimensions for visualization while preserving maximum variance. Which technique should they use?
questions.option_a: t-SNE
questions.option_b: UMAP
questions.option_c: Linear Discriminant Analysis
questions.option_d: Principal Component Analysis (PCA)
questions.explanation: PCA is a dimensionality reduction technique that projects data onto the directions (principal components) of maximum variance. When reducing to 2D for visualization, PCA is the primary linear method. t-SNE and UMAP are nonlinear techniques better suited for cluster visualization.

questions.statement: Which metric is most appropriate for evaluating a classification model when the dataset has a severe class imbalance, such as 99% negative and 1% positive cases?
questions.option_a: Accuracy
questions.option_b: Mean Squared Error
questions.option_c: F1-Score
questions.option_d: R-squared
questions.explanation: Accuracy is misleading for imbalanced datasets (a model predicting all negatives gets 99% accuracy). F1-Score balances Precision and Recall, giving a better picture of performance on the minority class. MSE and R-squared are regression metrics.

questions.statement: What does the acronym NLP stand for in artificial intelligence?
questions.option_a: Neural Language Processing
questions.option_b: Natural Logic Programming
questions.option_c: Natural Language Processing
questions.option_d: Normalized Linguistic Patterns
questions.explanation: NLP stands for Natural Language Processing, the subfield of AI concerned with enabling computers to understand, interpret, and generate human language. The other options are fabricated expansions of the same initials.

questions.statement: A company trains a sentiment analysis model on product reviews from 2018 but deploys it in 2024. The model's performance degrades over time as language use evolves. What phenomenon describes this degradation?
questions.option_a: Data leakage
questions.option_b: Model collapse
questions.option_c: Concept drift
questions.option_d: Feature drift
questions.explanation: Concept drift occurs when the statistical properties of the target variable change over time due to shifts in real-world conditions, causing model performance to degrade. Regular monitoring and retraining are required to address it.

questions.statement: In a confusion matrix for binary classification, what does 'False Positive' (FP) represent?
questions.option_a: The model correctly predicted a positive class
questions.option_b: The model predicted negative, but the actual class was positive
questions.option_c: The model predicted positive, but the actual class was negative
questions.option_d: The model correctly predicted a negative class
questions.explanation: A False Positive (FP) occurs when the model predicts the positive class but the actual label is negative (a false alarm). False Negative (FN) is the opposite: the model predicts negative when the actual is positive.

questions.statement: Which activation function is most commonly used in hidden layers of deep neural networks because it mitigates the vanishing gradient problem?
questions.option_a: Sigmoid
questions.option_b: Softmax
questions.option_c: Tanh
questions.option_d: ReLU
questions.explanation: ReLU (Rectified Linear Unit), f(x)=max(0,x), does not saturate for positive values, avoiding the vanishing gradient problem that plagues Sigmoid and Tanh. It is computationally efficient and the default choice for hidden layers.

questions.statement: A data analyst wants to understand the relationship and direction of association between two continuous numerical variables. Which statistical measure should they compute?
questions.option_a: Chi-squared statistic
questions.option_b: Pearson Correlation Coefficient
questions.option_c: Gini Impurity
questions.option_d: Euclidean Distance
questions.explanation: The Pearson Correlation Coefficient measures the strength and direction of the linear relationship between two continuous variables, ranging from -1 (perfect negative) to +1 (perfect positive). Chi-squared tests associations between categorical variables.

questions.statement: Which hyperparameter in a decision tree controls its complexity most directly by limiting how many levels it can grow?
questions.option_a: n_estimators
questions.option_b: min_samples_split
questions.option_c: max_features
questions.option_d: max_depth
questions.explanation: max_depth limits the maximum number of levels in a decision tree, directly controlling model complexity. A deeper tree is more complex and prone to overfitting; a shallower tree may underfit. min_samples_split controls the minimum samples needed to split a node.

questions.statement: In gradient boosting, how does each subsequent tree in the ensemble correct the errors of the previous ones?
questions.option_a: By training on a random bootstrap sample of the original data
questions.option_b: By training on the residual errors (gradients of the loss) left by the previous model
questions.option_c: By averaging the predictions of all previous trees
questions.option_d: By using a different subset of features than the previous tree
questions.explanation: Gradient Boosting trains each new tree on the residual errors (negative gradients of the loss function) of the ensemble so far. Each tree corrects the specific mistakes of its predecessors. This is distinct from Bagging, which trains trees independently on resampled data.

questions.statement: What does the term 'feature engineering' refer to in machine learning?
questions.option_a: Selecting the best machine learning algorithm for a given problem
questions.option_b: The process of creating, transforming, and selecting input variables to improve model performance
questions.option_c: Automatically learning features from raw data using deep neural networks
questions.option_d: Evaluating the importance of each feature using SHAP values
questions.explanation: Feature engineering is the domain-expertise-driven process of creating new features, transforming existing ones, or selecting the most relevant variables to provide better inputs to a machine learning model. Deep learning reduces but does not eliminate its need.

questions.statement: A neural network for image classification uses multiple convolutional layers. What is the primary purpose of these convolutional layers?
questions.option_a: To reduce the spatial dimensions of the image to a single vector
questions.option_b: To automatically learn spatial hierarchies of features like edges, textures, and shapes
questions.option_c: To normalize pixel values between 0 and 1 before classification
questions.option_d: To transform the image into frequency domain representations
questions.explanation: Convolutional layers apply learnable filters that detect spatial patterns such as edges (in early layers) and complex shapes (in deeper layers), enabling the network to automatically learn hierarchical visual features from raw pixel data.

questions.statement: Which unsupervised learning algorithm groups data points by measuring their similarity to evolving cluster centroids and reassigning points iteratively until convergence?
questions.option_a: DBSCAN
questions.option_b: Hierarchical Clustering
questions.option_c: K-Means Clustering
questions.option_d: Gaussian Mixture Model
questions.explanation: K-Means iteratively assigns each data point to the nearest centroid, recalculates centroid positions as the mean of assigned points, and repeats until assignments stabilize. DBSCAN groups points by density without requiring a pre-specified cluster count.

questions.statement: What is 'data leakage' in a machine learning pipeline?
questions.option_a: Data that is accidentally deleted during preprocessing
questions.option_b: The inclusion of information from the test or future data into the training process, leading to inflated evaluation metrics
questions.option_c: The loss of data during transmission from a sensor to a database
questions.option_d: The exposure of training data to external parties during model deployment
questions.explanation: Data leakage occurs when information that would not be available at prediction time is used during training, causing the model to appear highly accurate during evaluation but fail in production. Common sources include target-based encoding before splitting.

questions.statement: Which Python library is the primary ecosystem for building and training deep learning models from Google, offering both high-level Keras and low-level tensor APIs?
questions.option_a: PyTorch
questions.option_b: Scikit-learn
questions.option_c: MXNet
questions.option_d: TensorFlow
questions.explanation: TensorFlow is Google's open-source deep learning framework offering the high-level Keras API for rapid prototyping and lower-level APIs for custom model building. PyTorch is Meta's competing framework; Scikit-learn focuses on traditional ML algorithms.

questions.statement: What does the acronym CNN stand for in deep learning?
questions.option_a: Cascaded Node Network
questions.option_b: Convolutional Neural Network
questions.option_c: Clustered Neural Network
questions.option_d: Connected Node Network
questions.explanation: CNN stands for Convolutional Neural Network, a deep learning architecture designed for processing structured grid data such as images, using convolutional layers to automatically extract spatial features. The other options are fabricated expansions.

questions.statement: A data scientist applies Min-Max Scaling to a feature. What range of values will the transformed feature occupy?
questions.option_a: Between -1 and 1
questions.option_b: Between 0 and 100
questions.option_c: Between 0 and 1
questions.option_d: Between -3 and 3
questions.explanation: Min-Max Scaling (normalization) transforms feature values to the range [0, 1] using the formula: (x - min) / (max - min). Standardization (Z-score scaling) produces a mean of 0 and standard deviation of 1, not Min-Max.

questions.statement: In machine learning model evaluation, what does the ROC curve plot?
questions.option_a: Precision on the y-axis against Recall on the x-axis
questions.option_b: True Positive Rate (Sensitivity) on the y-axis against False Positive Rate on the x-axis
questions.option_c: Model accuracy on the y-axis against training dataset size on the x-axis
questions.option_d: Loss function value on the y-axis against training epochs on the x-axis
questions.explanation: The ROC (Receiver Operating Characteristic) curve plots the True Positive Rate (Recall/Sensitivity) against the False Positive Rate at various classification thresholds, visualizing the tradeoff between sensitivity and specificity.

questions.statement: Which ensemble learning technique trains multiple models sequentially, where each model learns from the mistakes of the previous one?
questions.option_a: Bagging
questions.option_b: Stacking
questions.option_c: Voting
questions.option_d: Boosting
questions.explanation: Boosting is a sequential ensemble method where each model is trained on the errors of its predecessor, with misclassified samples receiving higher weights in subsequent iterations. Bagging trains models in parallel on random data subsets.

questions.statement: A data engineer discovers that a dataset has duplicate records that represent the same real-world entity. Which data pre-processing step addresses this?
questions.option_a: Feature scaling
questions.option_b: Outlier detection and removal
questions.option_c: Deduplication
questions.option_d: Label encoding
questions.explanation: Deduplication identifies and removes duplicate records that represent the same entity, improving data quality and preventing over-representation of certain samples during model training.

questions.statement: What is the primary purpose of regularization techniques such as L1 (Lasso) and L2 (Ridge) in machine learning?
questions.option_a: To speed up model training by reducing the number of training iterations
questions.option_b: To reduce model complexity and prevent overfitting by adding a penalty for large weights
questions.option_c: To improve the interpretability of the model's feature importance scores
questions.option_d: To normalize the input feature distributions before training
questions.explanation: Regularization adds a penalty term to the loss function based on the magnitude of model weights, discouraging the model from assigning excessively large coefficients, thus reducing overfitting and improving generalization.

questions.statement: Which type of recurrent neural network architecture was specifically designed to solve the vanishing gradient problem in long sequences by using memory cells and gating mechanisms?
questions.option_a: Simple RNN
questions.option_b: Bidirectional RNN
questions.option_c: GRU (Gated Recurrent Unit)
questions.option_d: LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory)
questions.explanation: LSTM networks introduce a cell state and three gates (input, forget, output) that control what information is remembered or forgotten over long sequences, directly addressing the vanishing gradient problem of simple RNNs.

questions.statement: In the context of AI ethics, what is 'algorithmic bias'?
questions.option_a: The intentional selection of biased training data by malicious actors
questions.option_b: Systematic errors in model outputs that unfairly disadvantage certain groups due to biased training data or model design
questions.option_c: The natural tendency of neural networks to underfit complex data
questions.option_d: The computational overhead introduced by fairness constraints during training
questions.explanation: Algorithmic bias is the systematic tendency of an AI system to produce discriminatory or unfair outputs, often stemming from biased training data, biased feature selection, or flawed model design. It can perpetuate or amplify societal inequalities.

questions.statement: What does the acronym PCA stand for in dimensionality reduction?
questions.option_a: Partial Clustering Analysis
questions.option_b: Principal Component Analysis
questions.option_c: Probabilistic Classification Algorithm
questions.option_d: Parametric Correlation Analysis
questions.explanation: PCA stands for Principal Component Analysis, a technique that transforms data into a new coordinate system aligned with the directions of maximum variance, reducing dimensionality while retaining the most important information. The other options are fabricated.

questions.statement: A recommendation system suggests items to a user based on the preferences of other users with similar taste profiles. Which type of collaborative filtering is being used?
questions.option_a: Content-Based Filtering
questions.option_b: Matrix Factorization
questions.option_c: Item-Based Collaborative Filtering
questions.option_d: User-Based Collaborative Filtering
questions.explanation: User-Based Collaborative Filtering identifies users with similar preference patterns and recommends items that those similar users liked. Item-Based Collaborative Filtering instead finds items similar to those a user has already liked.

questions.statement: In natural language processing, what is the purpose of 'tokenization'?
questions.option_a: Converting text into dense vector embeddings for semantic similarity
questions.option_b: Splitting text into individual units (words, subwords, or characters) for further processing
questions.option_c: Removing stopwords and irrelevant terms from a text corpus
questions.option_d: Assigning part-of-speech tags to each word in a sentence
questions.explanation: Tokenization is the process of splitting a text string into smaller units called tokens (words, subwords, or characters). It is typically the first step in any NLP pipeline, converting raw text into a structured format for subsequent processing.

questions.statement: Which machine learning algorithm finds the optimal hyperplane that maximizes the margin between classes in a high-dimensional feature space?
questions.option_a: Logistic Regression
questions.option_b: K-Nearest Neighbors
questions.option_c: Naive Bayes
questions.option_d: Support Vector Machine (SVM)
questions.explanation: SVM finds the maximum-margin hyperplane—the decision boundary that maximizes the distance to the nearest training examples (support vectors) from each class. This maximization improves generalization to unseen data.

questions.statement: A company deploys a model that predicts employee attrition with 95% accuracy. However, the HR team complains the model rarely identifies actual employees who leave. What is most likely wrong?
questions.option_a: The model was trained on too much data
questions.option_b: The model is underfitting the training data
questions.option_c: The dataset is imbalanced and accuracy is a misleading metric
questions.option_d: The model was trained with too many features
questions.explanation: If the attrition rate is, say, 5%, a model predicting 'no attrition' for everyone achieves 95% accuracy but zero recall on the positive class. An imbalanced dataset requires metrics like F1, Precision, Recall, or AUC-ROC rather than accuracy.

questions.statement: Which Python library provides tools for building machine learning pipelines, preprocessing, and a wide range of classical algorithms including SVMs and random forests?
questions.option_a: TensorFlow
questions.option_b: Keras
questions.option_c: PyTorch
questions.option_d: Scikit-learn
questions.explanation: Scikit-learn is the go-to Python library for classical machine learning, providing consistent APIs for algorithms, preprocessing utilities, model selection tools, and pipeline construction. TensorFlow, Keras, and PyTorch are primarily for deep learning.

questions.statement: What is 'cross-validation' used for in machine learning model evaluation?
questions.option_a: Validating that the model's code runs without errors on different platforms
questions.option_b: Using the full dataset to train and evaluate the model more reliably by averaging results across multiple splits
questions.option_c: Comparing two different model architectures on the same test set
questions.option_d: Checking that the validation data has the same distribution as the training data
questions.explanation: Cross-validation (e.g., k-fold) splits the data into k subsets, trains on k-1 folds, and tests on the remaining fold, repeating k times. Averaging metrics across folds provides a more reliable performance estimate than a single train-test split.

questions.statement: In computer vision, which deep learning architecture introduced the concept of residual (skip) connections to enable training of very deep networks?
questions.option_a: VGG-16
questions.option_b: AlexNet
questions.option_c: ResNet (Residual Network)
questions.option_d: Inception Network
questions.explanation: ResNet, introduced by He et al. in 2015, uses shortcut (skip) connections that add the input of a layer block to its output, creating residual paths. This allows gradients to flow more easily and enables training of networks with hundreds of layers.

questions.statement: What does the acronym LSTM stand for in deep learning?
questions.option_a: Long-Scale Training Model
questions.option_b: Linear Sequential Transmission Module
questions.option_c: Large-Scale Text Model
questions.option_d: Long Short-Term Memory
questions.explanation: LSTM stands for Long Short-Term Memory, a type of recurrent neural network architecture with gating mechanisms designed to capture long-range dependencies in sequential data. The other options are fabricated expansions.

questions.statement: A data scientist computes the Pearson correlation coefficient between two features and gets a value of 0.02. What does this indicate?
questions.option_a: A strong positive linear relationship between the two features
questions.option_b: A strong negative linear relationship between the two features
questions.option_c: A near-zero linear relationship between the two features
questions.option_d: A perfect curvilinear relationship between the two features
questions.explanation: A Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.02 is very close to zero, indicating virtually no linear relationship between the two features. Note that this does not preclude a nonlinear relationship.

questions.statement: Which technique is used to explain the prediction of any machine learning model by assigning an importance value to each feature for a specific prediction?
questions.option_a: Permutation Feature Importance
questions.option_b: Partial Dependence Plot
questions.option_c: LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations) or SHAP
questions.option_d: Cross-Validation
questions.explanation: LIME and SHAP are model-agnostic explainability methods that assign importance scores to input features for individual predictions, helping interpret black-box model decisions. Permutation importance is a global measure, not per-prediction.

questions.statement: In the context of NLP, what is 'word embedding' and what advantage does it offer over one-hot encoding?
questions.option_a: A compression technique that reduces vocabulary size; advantage is smaller storage
questions.option_b: A dense vector representation that captures semantic and syntactic relationships; advantage is meaningful similarity between words
questions.option_c: A sparse binary vector; advantage is exact matching of words
questions.option_d: A character-level encoding; advantage is handling out-of-vocabulary words
questions.explanation: Word embeddings (e.g., Word2Vec, GloVe) represent words as dense vectors in a continuous space where semantically similar words are close together. Unlike one-hot encoding, they capture meaning relationships like 'king - man + woman ≈ queen'.

questions.statement: What is the purpose of the 'dropout' regularization technique in deep neural networks?
questions.option_a: To remove features with low variance from the input data before training
questions.option_b: To randomly deactivate a fraction of neurons during each training step to prevent co-adaptation
questions.option_c: To reduce the learning rate at scheduled intervals during training
questions.option_d: To clip gradient values to prevent exploding gradients
questions.explanation: Dropout randomly sets a fraction of neuron activations to zero during each training forward pass, forcing the network to learn redundant representations and preventing neurons from co-adapting, which reduces overfitting.

questions.statement: Which statistical test is used to determine if a difference in means between two independent groups is statistically significant?
questions.option_a: Chi-squared test
questions.option_b: ANOVA (Analysis of Variance)
questions.option_c: Mann-Whitney U test
questions.option_d: Independent samples t-test
questions.explanation: The independent samples t-test compares the means of two independent groups to determine if the observed difference is statistically significant. ANOVA compares means across three or more groups; Chi-squared tests categorical associations.

questions.statement: A company wants to group its customers into segments based on purchasing behavior without predefined categories. Which type of machine learning approach is appropriate?
questions.option_a: Supervised Classification
questions.option_b: Reinforcement Learning
questions.option_c: Regression Analysis
questions.option_d: Unsupervised Clustering
questions.explanation: Unsupervised Clustering (e.g., k-means, hierarchical clustering) identifies natural groupings in data without labels, making it appropriate for customer segmentation where the number and nature of segments are unknown in advance.

questions.statement: In reinforcement learning, what is the role of the 'reward signal'?
questions.option_a: It provides labeled training examples for the agent to learn from
questions.option_b: It measures the quality of the agent's actions and guides the learning process toward maximizing cumulative reward
questions.option_c: It initializes the weights of the neural network policy
questions.option_d: It defines the complete set of possible actions in the environment
questions.explanation: The reward signal in reinforcement learning provides feedback on the quality of the agent's actions in a given state. The agent learns a policy that maximizes the expected cumulative (discounted) reward over time.

questions.statement: What does the acronym GAN stand for in deep learning?
questions.option_a: Gradient Adversarial Network
questions.option_b: Generalized Attention Network
questions.option_c: Generative Adversarial Network
questions.option_d: Gradient Approximation Network
questions.explanation: GAN stands for Generative Adversarial Network, a deep learning framework where a generator network creates synthetic data and a discriminator network tries to distinguish it from real data, with both networks improving adversarially. The other options are fabricated.

questions.statement: A model trained on historical loan approval data learns to deny loans to applicants from a specific postal code regardless of their financial profile. This is an example of which AI risk?
questions.option_a: Model underfitting
questions.option_b: Proxy discrimination perpetuating historical bias
questions.option_c: Overfitting to outlier data points
questions.option_d: Catastrophic forgetting in the training process
questions.explanation: The model has learned to use postal code as a proxy for a protected characteristic (e.g., race), perpetuating historical discrimination in the training data. This is a form of proxy discrimination, an AI fairness and ethics concern.

questions.statement: Which evaluation metric measures the proportion of actual positive cases that the model correctly identified?
questions.option_a: Precision
questions.option_b: Specificity
questions.option_c: F1-Score
questions.option_d: Recall (Sensitivity)
questions.explanation: Recall (also called Sensitivity or True Positive Rate) = TP / (TP + FN). It measures the fraction of actual positive cases that the model correctly predicted as positive. Precision measures the fraction of predicted positives that are actually positive.

questions.statement: In the context of deep learning, what is 'transfer learning'?
questions.option_a: Transferring a trained model from one server to another for deployment
questions.option_b: Using a model pre-trained on a large dataset as a starting point for a related task with less data
questions.option_c: Transferring knowledge between multiple student-teacher neural network pairs
questions.option_d: Moving the training process from CPU to GPU
questions.explanation: Transfer learning leverages weights learned by a model on a large task (e.g., ImageNet classification) as an initialization for a new, related task (e.g., medical image classification), reducing the need for large labeled datasets.

questions.statement: A data scientist is asked to predict house prices based on features like size, location, and number of rooms. Which type of supervised learning task is this?
questions.option_a: Binary Classification
questions.option_b: Multi-class Classification
questions.option_c: Clustering
questions.option_d: Regression
questions.explanation: Predicting a continuous numerical output (house price) is a regression task. Classification tasks predict discrete categories. Clustering is an unsupervised task without a target variable.

questions.statement: What is the primary difference between L1 (Lasso) and L2 (Ridge) regularization?
questions.option_a: L1 uses the squared sum of weights; L2 uses the absolute sum of weights
questions.option_b: L1 adds absolute weight values to the loss, driving some weights to zero; L2 adds squared weight values, shrinking all weights without eliminating features
questions.option_c: L1 only applies to linear models; L2 applies to all model types
questions.option_d: L1 reduces bias; L2 reduces variance independently
questions.explanation: L1 (Lasso) regularization adds the sum of absolute weight values (L1 norm) to the loss, which can drive some weights to exactly zero (feature selection). L2 (Ridge) adds the sum of squared weights (L2 norm), which shrinks weights but rarely to exactly zero.

questions.statement: Which technique in NLP converts text into a matrix where each row is a document and each column is a word, with values representing word frequency?
questions.option_a: Word2Vec
questions.option_b: TF-IDF
questions.option_c: Bag of Words (BoW)
questions.option_d: BERT Embeddings
questions.explanation: The Bag of Words model represents each document as a vector where each element counts the occurrence of a word from the vocabulary. It ignores word order. TF-IDF extends BoW by weighting words by their document frequency.

questions.statement: What does the acronym AUC-ROC stand for in model evaluation?
questions.option_a: Automated Uniform Curve - Rate of Convergence
questions.option_b: Area Under the Curve - Receiver Operating Characteristic
questions.option_c: Adaptive Update Cycle - Recall-Oriented Computation
questions.option_d: Average Utility Coefficient - Robust Output Classification
questions.explanation: AUC-ROC stands for Area Under the Curve of the Receiver Operating Characteristic curve. It measures the model's ability to discriminate between classes across all thresholds; an AUC of 1.0 is perfect, 0.5 is no better than random.

questions.statement: In big data analytics, what do the three V's of big data primarily refer to?
questions.option_a: Visualization, Verification, and Velocity
questions.option_b: Volume, Velocity, and Variety
questions.option_c: Value, Validity, and Veracity
questions.option_d: Volume, Validation, and Virtualization
questions.explanation: The three V's of big data are Volume (large quantities of data), Velocity (the speed at which data is generated and processed), and Variety (the different types and formats of data). Some frameworks extend this to 5 V's adding Veracity and Value.

questions.statement: A data scientist notices that a feature 'number of bedrooms' has a value of 500 in some records for residential houses. How should this be treated?
questions.option_a: Replaced with the mean value of the column
questions.option_b: Kept as is to preserve all available data points
questions.option_c: Investigated and treated as a potential outlier or data entry error
questions.option_d: Removed by dropping the entire column
questions.explanation: A value of 500 bedrooms for a residential house is implausible and likely a data entry error. Outliers should be investigated in context before applying treatment (removal, capping, or correction) to avoid corrupting the model.

questions.statement: Which deep learning technique adds random noise or makes small perturbations to training images to make the model more robust to variations?
questions.option_a: Batch Normalization
questions.option_b: Dropout
questions.option_c: Gradient Clipping
questions.option_d: Data Augmentation
questions.explanation: Data augmentation artificially expands the training dataset by applying random transformations (flips, rotations, crops, color jitter) to images, helping the model generalize to variations it may encounter in real-world data.

questions.statement: What is the purpose of the 'learning rate' hyperparameter in gradient descent optimization?
questions.option_a: To define the proportion of training data used in each mini-batch
questions.option_b: To control the step size taken in the direction of the negative gradient when updating weights
questions.option_c: To set the number of hidden layers in a neural network
questions.option_d: To determine how many training epochs will be run before early stopping
questions.explanation: The learning rate determines how large a step gradient descent takes in the direction of the negative gradient at each update. Too high a learning rate causes instability; too low a rate causes slow convergence or getting stuck in local minima.

questions.statement: In NLP, the Transformer architecture introduced in 'Attention is All You Need' relies on which core mechanism for relating different positions in a sequence?
questions.option_a: Convolutional Filters
questions.option_b: Recurrent Processing
questions.option_c: Self-Attention (Scaled Dot-Product Attention)
questions.option_d: Capsule Routing
questions.explanation: The Transformer architecture replaces recurrence with a Self-Attention mechanism that computes a weighted representation of all positions in the sequence simultaneously, allowing it to capture long-range dependencies more effectively than RNNs.

questions.statement: What does MLOps stand for and what is its primary goal?
questions.option_a: Multi-Layer Operations; reducing neural network depth for deployment
questions.option_b: Machine Learning Operations; streamlining the lifecycle of ML models from development to production
questions.option_c: Model Learning Optimization; tuning hyperparameters in production
questions.option_d: Machine Language Operations; translating model code between frameworks
questions.explanation: MLOps stands for Machine Learning Operations, a set of practices that combines machine learning, DevOps, and data engineering to automate and streamline the entire ML lifecycle—from data preparation and training to deployment and monitoring.

questions.statement: A company trains a sentiment classifier on customer reviews from its website. When deployed on social media comments, performance drops significantly. What is the root cause?
questions.option_a: The social media dataset is too large for the model
questions.option_b: The model has memorized the training data and is overfitting
questions.option_c: The model was trained and tested on data from different distributions (domain shift)
questions.option_d: The model lacks sufficient hidden layers for text processing
questions.explanation: Domain shift (or distribution shift) occurs when the training and deployment data come from different distributions. A model trained on formal website reviews may fail on informal social media language, slang, and emojis.

questions.statement: Which type of neural network architecture is primarily designed for processing sequential data such as time series, speech, and text?
questions.option_a: Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)
questions.option_b: Generative Adversarial Network (GAN)
questions.option_c: Recurrent Neural Network (RNN)
questions.option_d: Autoencoder
questions.explanation: Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) process sequential data by maintaining a hidden state that captures information from previous time steps, making them suited for tasks involving temporal or sequential dependencies.

questions.statement: What does the acronym BERT stand for in NLP?
questions.option_a: Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers
questions.option_b: Batch Embedding Recurrent Transformer
questions.option_c: Bidirectional Evaluation and Recall Technique
questions.option_d: Basic Embedding Representation Tokenizer
questions.explanation: BERT stands for Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers. It pre-trains deep bidirectional Transformer representations by jointly conditioning on both left and right context, achieving state-of-the-art results on many NLP tasks.

questions.statement: A data analyst calculates a p-value of 0.003 for a hypothesis test at a significance level of 0.05. What is the correct interpretation?
questions.option_a: Fail to reject the null hypothesis because p < 0.05
questions.option_b: Reject the null hypothesis because p < 0.05, indicating statistical significance
questions.option_c: Accept the null hypothesis because the result is less than the threshold
questions.option_d: Reject the alternative hypothesis because p is very small
questions.explanation: A p-value of 0.003 is less than the significance level of 0.05, which means we reject the null hypothesis. The result is statistically significant, indicating the observed data is unlikely under the null hypothesis.

questions.statement: What is 'batch normalization' in deep learning and what problem does it solve?
questions.option_a: A technique for training on mini-batches of data; it solves slow training due to small datasets
questions.option_b: A layer that normalizes activations within each mini-batch; it stabilizes and accelerates training by reducing internal covariate shift
questions.option_c: A method of normalizing gradient values to prevent explosion; it solves numerical instability
questions.option_d: A technique for normalizing input features before feeding them into the network; it eliminates the need for data preprocessing
questions.explanation: Batch Normalization normalizes the activations of each layer across the mini-batch to have zero mean and unit variance, reducing internal covariate shift, stabilizing training, allowing higher learning rates, and reducing sensitivity to weight initialization.

questions.statement: Which technique is used to automatically search for the optimal set of hyperparameters for a machine learning model?
questions.option_a: Cross-Validation
questions.option_b: Feature Selection
questions.option_c: Hyperparameter Tuning (e.g., Grid Search or Bayesian Optimization)
questions.option_d: Transfer Learning
questions.explanation: Hyperparameter tuning systematically searches over a hyperparameter space (e.g., Grid Search exhaustively, Random Search randomly, or Bayesian Optimization intelligently) to find the combination that maximizes validation performance.

questions.statement: In the context of data analytics, what is an 'outlier'?
questions.option_a: A missing value that needs to be imputed before model training
questions.option_b: A data point that differs significantly from other observations in the dataset
questions.option_c: A feature with very low correlation to the target variable
questions.option_d: A data record that exists in both the training and test sets
questions.explanation: An outlier is a data point that lies far from the bulk of the data distribution. Outliers can result from measurement errors, data entry mistakes, or genuinely rare events, and they can significantly affect statistical analyses and model training.

questions.statement: What is the difference between 'precision' and 'recall' in classification model evaluation?
questions.option_a: Precision measures the proportion of positive predictions that are correct; recall measures the proportion of actual positives the model identified
questions.option_b: Precision measures model accuracy on the training set; recall measures accuracy on the test set
questions.option_c: Precision is a metric for regression; recall is a metric for binary classification
questions.option_d: Precision measures the True Negative Rate; recall measures the True Positive Rate
questions.explanation: Precision = TP / (TP + FP) — of all predicted positives, how many are correct. Recall = TP / (TP + FN) — of all actual positives, how many did the model find. They are often in tension, and F1-Score balances them.

questions.statement: What does the acronym SVM stand for?
questions.option_a: Supervised Vector Model
questions.option_b: Statistical Variance Minimizer
questions.option_c: Stochastic Variance Machine
questions.option_d: Support Vector Machine
questions.explanation: SVM stands for Support Vector Machine, a supervised learning algorithm that finds the maximum-margin hyperplane to separate classes. The other options are fabricated expansions of the same initials.

questions.statement: A data scientist is selecting features for a model and identifies two features with a Pearson correlation of 0.98 with each other. What problem might including both features cause?
questions.option_a: Underfitting due to insufficient feature diversity
questions.option_b: Multicollinearity, which can destabilize coefficient estimates in linear models
questions.option_c: Data leakage from one feature into the other
questions.option_d: Overfitting due to too many training samples
questions.explanation: Multicollinearity occurs when two or more features are highly linearly correlated. In linear and logistic regression, this can cause unstable and unreliable coefficient estimates, making individual feature importance difficult to interpret.

questions.statement: Which evaluation metric for regression models measures the proportion of the variance in the dependent variable that is explained by the independent variables?
questions.option_a: Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE)
questions.option_b: Mean Absolute Error (MAE)
questions.option_c: R-squared (Coefficient of Determination)
questions.option_d: Mean Squared Error (MSE)
questions.explanation: R-squared measures the proportion of total variance in the target variable explained by the model, ranging from 0 (no explanatory power) to 1 (perfect fit). RMSE and MAE measure the magnitude of prediction errors in the original units.

questions.statement: A machine learning engineer deploys a model as a REST API endpoint. Which format is most commonly used to send input data and receive predictions in this context?
questions.option_a: CSV (Comma-Separated Values)
questions.option_b: Parquet
questions.option_c: XML (Extensible Markup Language)
questions.option_d: JSON (JavaScript Object Notation)
questions.explanation: JSON is the standard data interchange format for REST APIs due to its lightweight, human-readable structure and native support in web languages. CSV and Parquet are file-based formats better suited for bulk data storage and transfer.

questions.statement: In feature engineering, what is 'one-hot encoding' used for?
questions.option_a: Converting continuous numerical features into categorical bins
questions.option_b: Converting ordinal categorical features into integer ranks
questions.option_c: Normalizing numerical features to the range [0, 1]
questions.option_d: Converting nominal categorical variables into binary dummy variables
questions.explanation: One-hot encoding converts a nominal categorical variable (with no inherent order) into a set of binary (0/1) dummy variables, one per category. This allows categorical data to be used in algorithms that require numerical inputs without implying an ordinal relationship.

questions.statement: What is the 'curse of dimensionality' in machine learning?
questions.option_a: The tendency of models to curse or discard low-variance features during training
questions.option_b: The phenomenon where data becomes increasingly sparse and distance-based models lose effectiveness as the number of dimensions grows
questions.option_c: The exponential increase in training time caused by using GPU acceleration
questions.option_d: The problem of having too few samples in high-dimensional spaces for gradient descent to converge
questions.explanation: The curse of dimensionality describes how high-dimensional spaces become exponentially sparse—all data points become roughly equidistant, making distance-based algorithms like KNN ineffective. Feature selection and dimensionality reduction are common remedies.

questions.statement: Which Python function from Pandas is used to check for the number of missing values in each column of a DataFrame?
questions.option_a: df.describe()
questions.option_b: df.info()
questions.option_c: df.isna().sum()
questions.option_d: df.value_counts()
questions.explanation: df.isna().sum() returns a Series with the count of missing (NaN) values for each column in the DataFrame. df.info() shows non-null counts but df.isna().sum() provides a direct, column-wise missing value count.

questions.statement: What is 'early stopping' as a regularization technique in neural network training?
questions.option_a: Stopping training when the gradient magnitude drops below a defined threshold
questions.option_b: Monitoring validation loss during training and stopping when it begins to increase to prevent overfitting
questions.option_c: Reducing the learning rate after a fixed number of epochs
questions.option_d: Limiting the number of training examples used per epoch
questions.explanation: Early stopping monitors the validation loss throughout training. When the validation loss stops improving or begins to increase (indicating overfitting), training is stopped. The model from the best validation epoch is kept.

questions.statement: Which probability theorem forms the mathematical foundation of Naive Bayes classifiers?
questions.option_a: The Central Limit Theorem
questions.option_b: Bayes' Theorem
questions.option_c: The Law of Large Numbers
questions.option_d: The Markov Property
questions.explanation: Naive Bayes classifiers are based on Bayes' Theorem: P(class | features) = P(features | class) * P(class) / P(features). The 'Naive' assumption is that all features are conditionally independent given the class, simplifying computation.

questions.statement: A data analyst discovers that the 'age' column in a dataset contains values such as -5 and 300. Which data quality issue does this represent?
questions.option_a: Missing data
questions.option_b: Data imbalance
questions.option_c: Invalid or erroneous data violating domain constraints
questions.option_d: Duplicate records
